#3914. Grand Theft Auto 6 becomes the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history

UPDATE: And the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store history.

UPDATE 11TH NOVEMBER: Grand Theft Auto 6 has also become the most pre-ordered game "of all time" on the Xbox Store, Microsoft has announced. And on that platform, again, the advice is to pre-load because of "unprecedented demand" for the game, a post on Xbox Wire said.

The Xbox difference is that you can use Xbox Cloud to stream GTA 6 to other Xbox devices, although not PC, notably - the game isn't available on PC and presumably Rockstar doesn't want it playable there by any means. Microsoft's stream-deal with Rockstar has also expanded to include Red Dead Redemption 2 "and more", which will be available to stream in the "coming months".

ORIGINAL STORY 10TH NOVEMBER: Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". Note, it's not the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation history, just on its digital PlayStation Store.

The announcement, which comes as Sony prepares to ditch physical releases for an all-digital future, was made in a PlayStation Blog post confirming pre-loads for GTA 6 are now live.

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store," Sony wrote. "Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start pre-loading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day.

"We strongly advise that everyone who is hoping to play on launch day to pre-load the game as soon as possible," the blog post added. So: consider yourselves advised.

GTA 6 becomes available as soon as your region's clock ticks over from midnight into 19th November, which, if you're in New Zealand, means you'll play the game before everyone else. If only there were a way to pretend you lived there...

Elsewhere in the blog post, Sony underlined some features coming specially to GTA 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro. On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported, but not - sadly - to PC.

Last night, in a Take-Two financial earnings call, company leader Strauss Zelnick said pre-orders for GTA 6 are tracking "far above expectations" and that soon, "numbers will speak for themselves". Presumably because they will be gripped by an excited form of sentience. It's expected that GTA 6 could become the best-selling instalment in an already mega-selling series; Zelnick reckons GTA 6 will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two in terms of success.

#3913. Marathon is becoming a whole new game next month with a roguelite PvE mode, a beta for a very Halo-esque team deathmatch mode, a vibey social space and more

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their plans for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

The previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

#3911. Here's our second wave of PS Plus games for November 2026 - and Sony's scrapping its barely used PC app

Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall!

Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach.

Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November:

And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November:

There's a lot to recommend in that list. Death Stranding 2 was one of the standout games of 2025. "A busier, louder, and more emotionally resplendent take on this singular hiking sim," Lewis Gordon wrote in Eurogamer's Death Stranding 2 review.

Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review.

Meanwhile, Atomfall - Rebellion's quirky British take on a Fallout-like post-apocalyptic idea - was awarded three out of five stars. "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review. It's presumably been significantly patched and smoothed since then.

The Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake also scored three out of five stars. "Some excellent enhancements make this the ultimate version of Dragon Quest 3, but it could still do more to make it wholly welcoming to newcomers," Daniella Lucas wrote in Eurogamer's Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D review.

We didn't review Hell Let Loose, but the popular World War 2 shooter would go on to amass a serious following and spawn a follow-up game in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam recently, which we did review. "The lavish jungles, rigid command structure, and emphasis on communication make Hell Let Loose: Vietnam a fascinating war simulator when it works. But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote.

There's plenty to be getting on with, then.

Sony also announced in the PlayStation Blog post it's retiring the PS Plus app on PC from 10th December. Why? Because nobody really uses it.

"With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. "As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

#3910. Ahead of GTA 6 and as concerns over genAI PC ports grow, Take-Two's CEO says they're revving up their "technical defences" and "legal activites" over piracy

"[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that"

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business issues they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended."

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

#3909. GTA 6 release day live coverage – all the latest news and updates

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's weird to type this out, but the GTA 6 release is finally upon us after a 13-year wait.

Red Dead Redemption 2 launched to acclaim at the time to ease the wait, though few things in gaming feel as big an event as a Grand Theft Auto release from Rockstar.

And thankfully, the wait looks to be worth it. The GamesRadar+ GTA 6 review lands on a perfect score, and says "Rockstar hasn't just set a new benchmark, it has delivered the highest-fidelity sandbox of the generation." It's not just us, either. The GTA 6 Metacritic score is a good 'un. In fact, only the OG Zelda: Ocarina of Time can match it.

So, we're probably on the same page. It's time to get the download going, and thoughts to our gaming brethren on PC who don't own a console.

To celebrate the moment, we're firing up the live blog to put everything you need to know in one, evolving space – from review buzz to launch requirements to exactly how the GTA 6 release time rollout is working. On that note, let's crack on.

And here we go! It may be GTA 6 release time for some sooner than others, but we'll all end up there eventually, right? So let's get into some things you'll need to know.

First things first. The main talking point today, as we count down the hours to launch, is critics' verdicts on GTA 6. As per our own GTA 6 review, we've landed on a perfect score.

"GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation," he says. "Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past installments."

We're not the only ones who dig this one either. The GTA 6 Metacritic score ranks it among the most popular games of all time. The only competition is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The original one, that is. Mind you, the remake is pretty nifty, too.

So! The game is good, though I have an inkling that plenty of you have already pre-ordered it. According to Sensor Tower, Rockstar has already made $1.45 billion from GTA 6, aided by nearly 90% of us buying the controversial $100 Ultimate Edition. Oof!

I imagine a few more people will be tossing some more money Rockstar's way.

So, for many of you who are jumping in, some housekeeping. First, the GTA 6 release time.

Rockstar isn't setting a singular time for people to jump in, so some of you will be playing sooner than others. Namely, congratulations to those of you who live in New Zealand or who know the trick. If you don't, our guide on how to play GTA 6 early with the New Zealand trick will sort you out.

If you've got some hours to wait, you're not alone. That said, you can still be productive. There's a new PS5 update you'll need to download to play GTA 6.

Sony hasn't confirmed what's behind the update, though we've got a good guess. Amid an AI explosion, PS5 jailbreaks have become more frequent in the run-up to GTA 6. Not only does that risk the latest Grand Theft Auto game being released before its official release date, but it could also result in it unofficially ending up on PC. Not ideal, no.

As we near release, though, it looks like Sony has managed ot hold this one off.

If you weren't already convinced, the GTA 6 reviews put Rockstar's latest in a good position for the upcoming Game Awards. Just yesterday, we found out that GTA 6 is up for several awards, including Game of the Year.

While that has led a few people to ask how that can be the case when it's not out yet, host Geoff Keighley has chimed in to add that reviewers behind the nominations have been playing it for three weeks. So, there is some reasoning to the inclusion.

You know it's a big day when none other than Rockstar president Sam Houser issues a rare statement. Here it is in full:

"Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with all of us.

"This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special. Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world full of possibilities — and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes. We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun.

"We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you."

As we wind down the live blog for the day, here's a fun one for you. One of the many mad details of GTA 6 is that all of its refrigerators sound different. It's all in the details, baby.

"Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," says audio VP Alastair MacGregor.

"One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect.

"As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment."

Game of the year, people. Game of the year.

#3908. Sony have cancelled Fairgame$, once again reminding us that chasing live service big bucks basically never works

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

#3907. PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away

After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff.

According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff.

"Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities".

Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue.

Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely. Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December.

The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026, following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond.

Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles, Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release.

Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May, but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

The Game Awards 2026 has just announced the nominees across all its categories, and sticking out like a sore thumb is GTA 6.

In fact, it's the most-nominated game at this year's awards, with a total of eight nods if you include Manni L. Perez's nomination for Best Performance. It's up for the following trophies:

Yes, on top of all its other nominations, GTA 6 is in contention for Game of the Year.

There has been much debate online about whether the game would be considered for The Game Awards at all, given how close its launch is to the event itself.

Many believed it would not receive any nominations, because the nominee announcement was set to occur before GTA 6 launches.

However, the voting jury — which comprises hundreds of gaming media outlets from around the world — has deemed the game worthy of recognition in eight categories, more than any other 2026 title.

What's clear is that many jury members must have played the game, but more interesting is that they clearly hold it in high regard if it's been shortlisted for so many awards.

This has been quite revealing, then; it's a big hint at what critics think of the game, and we now also know (officially) who is playing the role of Lucia Caminos, one of the two lead characters.

#3905. Three Big Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.

Feature GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?

Digital FoundryResolution, performance and visual settings compared.

Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.

This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.

Digital Foundry reckons that the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 is a great-looking game for the most part, highlighting things like lighting, reflections and even the incredible hair system, while also pointing out minor downsides such as missing shadows and occasionally blurry appearances. They also reckon that the frame rate generally maintains its 30FPS target, but will slip in busy situations like chases and explosions.

"Generally speaking, the game acquits itself quite well on Microsoft's senior current-gen console. Visual settings seem pretty solid across the board."

The Xbox Series S version is also said to be pretty good in the graphical department, retaining the core features that make GTA 6 such a great game visually. It's the frame rate that bothers DF the most, as it's much more variable and prone to falling below its 30FPS target. That said, it appears to hover around 25-30FPS for the most part.

"Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land."

If you're wondering which console is the absolute best to play GTA 6 on, it's unsurprisingly the PS5 Pro. Nevertheless, Digital Foundry says that both the Xbox Series X and the PS5 versions "look and play well" despite their softer image (and the Series X is actually "slightly smoother" when setting the Xbox to 120Hz with a VRR display), while the Xbox Series S version is the "hardest to recommend" despite its surprisingly impressive visuals.

"In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through."

Both the video and the website article are totally different from each other, so it's worth watching / reading the pair of them and getting a better idea of how GTA 6 fares across both Xbox consoles (and PS5 for that matter).

In my experience, I've found GTA 6 to be fantastic on Xbox Series X across the board for the most part, and while the Series S version is clearly a little more unstable, I'd wager that most players will still be perfectly happy with it.

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

Feature 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

The fun stuff that cropped up along the way, avoiding major story spoilers

#3904. What are Criminal Profiles in GTA 6?

Your Criminal Profile in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your reputation, similar to an honor or morality system

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Actions have consequences in Grand Theft Auto 6. Building on the honor system in Red Dead Redemption 2, fully functional Criminal Profiles in GTA 6 not only keep track of the way that you're playing the game, but help dictate how the world (and the characters who inhabit it) react to Jason and Lucia's presence.

GTA 6 Criminal Profiles are a really important metric that can change fundamental aspects of your play experience. I'm going to help you understand all of this with an overview of the Criminal Profiles in GTA 6, and offer up some tips on how you can change through the five tiers.

Your actions and behavior are captured in real-time by the Criminal Profile system. You are able to quickly check the status of your current criminal profile for both Jason and Lucia by holding right on the d-pad – look for the little icons next to their profile pictures for an update at a glance.

For a deeper dive navigate to the "Jason & Lucia" menu. These profiles change over time, and their status can have a lasting impact on each of the characters so you will want to check this frequently.

Jason and Lucia each have their own individual Criminal Profiles, but the actions of one character can influence the behavior of the other when you're out on the streets together.

There are five Criminal Profiles in GTA 6 that Lucia and Jason can move between, all of which are laid out below from least to most severe.

It's possible to move freely between Professional, Hardened, Violent, and Psycho tiers. However, should you create enough chaos to be considered Irredeemable this is an irreversible trait – and one which may permanently impact your relationship status in GTA 6.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Professional and Hardened Criminal Profiles are assigned to characters who do their best to avoid violence, and at least attempt to resolve situations without incident. Start pursuing extreme violence and cruelty to both animals and civilians and you'll become to etch into Violent and Psycho territories.

While you're on a mission, Criminal Profiles aren't affected by any criminal acts that the game requires you to do. It's only when you go beyond what is truly necessary or reasonable that action begins to have consequences in either direction.

Below your health bar is where the GTA 6 flashes up little icons which denote how your actions are impacting your criminal profile. The game will track low-casualty incursions and clean getaways, just as it will acts of extreme violence and destruction.

If your character is going in a direction you aren't happy with, here's what to be aware of with each Criminal Profile:

If you're after a Criminal Profile that lists you as a 'Professional' then you'll need to be considerate of your actions. Avoid casualties where possible, don't chase unnecessary aggression, and only do what could be considered reasonable to get the task at hand completed.

It's worth noting that making threats won't impact your Professional Criminal Profile, and that the best way to maintain this reputation is to avoid violence unless you're threatened and to try to remain undetected while committing crimes. This isn't always possible, just don't escalate for the sake of it.

Tip: Non-lethal incapacitations (aiming for joints rather than the head or heart), thoughtful actions, and petting every dog and cat you come across will increase your Focus in GTA 6 while you have a Professional Criminal Profile.

If you've found yourself with a Hardened Criminal Profile in GTA 6, it probably means that you've started to resort to violence to complete your objectives. Rushing to kill enemies and breaking detection for the sake of it will contribute to this profile – although it's still easy enough to get back to a Professional Criminal Profile if you take steps to avoid violence in a couple of robberies.

If you continue down this path, harming civilians and killing cops, then your Criminal Profile will eventually shift from Hardened to Violent. It's worth flagging that, like the Professional profile, non-lethal incapacitations will still contribute to an increase in your focus.

If you've gotten yourself a Violent Criminal Profile in GTA 6 then something has gone really wrong. This is the game reflecting that you've probably spent a fair few hours attacking cops and civilians for the smallest infractions. Brutally attacking cops and shooting fleeing civilians in the back will contribute to your Violent profile but acting in a self-defensive capacity will not.

If you find yourself pushing into Psycho territory, it is still possible to move back to Hardened or Professional. You'll just need to be more conscious about the way you are interacting with the world, and become more deliberate with your actions.

Tip: Headshots will increase your focus if you've gotten yourself a Violent profile, but each one of those will also make it more difficult to return to Hardened or Professional state.

You know what you're doing, and you don't care who knows about it. If you get assigned the Psycho Criminal Profile in GTA 6 then you've most likely spent a few hours mercilessly harming vulnerable animals (yes, hunting does count in certain instances), murdering defenseless civilians with abandon, and have been blasting through cops with no hesitation.

Something to note with the Psycho profile is that there is an additional icon you should keep an eye out for. If you see a line-scratch through the icon, it means you've reached a breaking point and are at risk of tipping into Irredeemable territory. Start shooting to incapacitate to get back to being a reasonable member of society.

If you continue acting with wild abandon once you reach the breaking point within the Psycho boundaries, eventually you will earn yourself an Irredeemable Criminal Profile in GTA 6. This is only given to the worst of the worst – this would have been Trevor's starting point in GTA 5 – and reflects your insistence on creating maximum chaos, regardless of the cost.

This level of excessive violence will make you irredeemable, which is permanently attributed to your character. This will impact the way civilians react to you on the street, it will drive a wedge between Jason and Lucia, and will change the way cops approach you too. If you've got a Psycho or Irredeemable Criminal Profile, expect cops to start open firing at you far faster than before.

Having a Psycho or Irredeemable profile will mean that headshots increase your focus, which is a great way to engage in gunplay. However, you'll also lose the ability to surrender to the cops – which can have a pretty big impact on your money in GTA 6.

#3903. Sick BMX flips, colourful characters, a whole lot of mail and a charming raccoon dog await you in Tanuki: Pon's Summer, which you can pick up now

Right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

When it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

There are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

#3902. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells in huge numbers, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days.

Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds.

It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6, eh?

This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity?

If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

GTA 6 cheat codes let you switch things up in Leonida, but you can't use them until you complete the story

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 cheats are here to let you cause the maximum amount of chaos possible in Leonida. Whether you're looking to raise up your Wanted Level and unlock infinite ammo just to see what happens, or testing out some base jump locations with no fall damage, cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 are what you're looking for.

A total of 61 GTA 6 cheats are available for PS5 and Xbox Series X, but you won't be able to use any of them right from the beginning of your adventures in Vice City. You need to fully complete Jason and Lucia's main story for cheat codes in GTA 6 to even activate, and from there you have to complete a series of challenges to unlock the codes themselves. It's a lot of work to go through in GTA 6, but trust me, it's worth it in the end.

As expected, once you have activated a cheat in GTA 6 all Trophies or Achievements are disabled for the duration of the play session – the ability to save the game will be disabled too. But with all of that out of the way, here are the GTA 6 cheats we have found so far.This guide is in-progress and will be updated as more GTA 6 cheat codes are unlocked.

GTA 6 cheats are only accessible after you complete all of the main missions. Once you've wrapped up Jason and Lucia's story, open the main menu with the touchpad or menu button and then press R1/RB to navigate to the Progress tab. In there you'll find a new option for Cheats in GTA 6 that wasn't there before.

GTA 6 cheats will not work until you have completed Jason and Lucia's story, regardless of whether you know the code already.

Using Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats is easy enough. While you're in free-roam, all you have to do is press Up on the D-pad to pull out your phone. From that main phone screen, you then need to hold L1/LB and R1/RB together at the same time, before inputting the relevant GTA 6 cheat code with the D-pad to activate it.

#3900. Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell says. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio."

Just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.)

None of this is intended to be a knock on Dawn of War 4. From what I've played it's a very good Warhammer 40K RTS, if it perhaps sticks a little closely to the model laid down by Relic's original. What do I know, though, talking about their own games, Dowdeswell tells me that while "one of the messages to the studio is we can't just make [the same] things that we made 20 years ago and hope it goes well", re-releasing the 20-year-old Dawn of War sold very well for Relic and netted the team some very positive reviews on Steam. "There's a bit of a paradox there," he adds"

Anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell says. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it."

Relic and new owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Company of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly."

I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a big part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a new game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future."

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer."

#3899. Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now just hours away! We're in the final home stretch now, with availability rolling out on PS5 worldwide within the next 24 hours.

As the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times.

On this page: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. If you have preloaded the game, it'll unlock at midnight, and then you can begin playing immediately.

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

As such, the game will unlock and be available first in New Zealand. Availability will then roll out worldwide as each time zone reaches midnight on 19th November.

When the game launches in the UK, we'll have a hub live on the home page documenting our coverage and providing a place for you to share your first experiences with GTA 6.

GTA 6 preload is available now! If you've pre-ordered from the PS Store, your download of the game should have started and will then be ready for you to start playing at release.

Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.

GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in New Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.

Because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating New Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.

When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the New Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.

If you were to play GTA 6 early via the New Zealand method detailed above, you get access to the game at these times:North America: 3am PST / 4am MST / 5am CST / 6am ESTUK/Ire: 11am GMTEurope: 12pm CET / 1pm EETAsia/Oceania: 8pm JST / 7pm AWST / 10pm AEDT

GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.

The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

Ultimate Edition / Ultimate Edition Upgrade Contents:

Rockstar is only selling GTA 6 in a digital format; you can't buy the game on a physical disc in any way. Even the version you buy in retail shops or from online retailers won't contain a disc. Instead, the actual GTA 6 box will have a code inside you can use to download the game. There's no version with a physical disc of any kind.

Rockstar has now confirmed a GTA 6 map will be made available, but it won't be included in the physical versions like for previous games. Instead, a physical GTA 6 map will be put on the official Rockstar store for $0.99. Or, it'll be included for free in all other purchases from the storefront.

Have you pre-ordered GTA 6, and will you be staying up to play at midnight? Let us know in the comments below.

#3898. Multiple Games Are Available Today On Xbox, Including One With GTA & Zelda Inspirations (November 18)

Just in case you wanted a break from the GTA news, we thought we'd remind you that we've got a few games either releasing or being added to Xbox Game Pass today, and there's some interesting stuff in the mix here.

The one that catches the eye is Vice: Magic City Mayhem, which we mentioned recently in our article about two Vice City games releasing in mid-November. While the cover art is very GTA-inspired, and it's set in a world with a "Vice City theme", it actually appears to have more in common with classic Zelda in terms of the gameplay style.

It's also a very temporary Xbox and and Epic Games Store exclusive, as the Steam, PS5 and Nintendo Switch versions have been slightly delayed for whatever reason.

News Xbox Suddenly Has Two Vice City Games Releasing In Mid-November

This one's based on Zelda with GTA influences!

Beyond this, three games are being added to the Xbox Game Pass Premium service today, with High on Life 2 arguably being the highlight (if you enjoy the kind of humour it throws at you). The other two are Call of the Elder Gods and Roadside Research, which are both worth a play as well.

GTA 6 is technically already out in some countries as well (such as New Zealand), but its official release date is November 19th rather than the 18th, so we'll highlight it in tomorrow's article instead.

We'll throw all of today's new Xbox releases and Xbox Game Pass additions down below.

Vice: Magic City Mayhem is a top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme. Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure.

Turn-based management roguelike. Command the Inquisition and rule an industrial city on the empire’s edge. Use your train to meet prisoner shipment quotas by hunting heretics and slaying magical beasts. Produce supplies, contain revolt, and sacrifice prisoners to stop the madness.

An intergalactic conspiracy threatens the fate of humanity! Team up with a wide cast of talking alien guns as you shoot, stab, and skate your way through the exotic locales to take down the bad guys and save your favorite species (humans)!

Journey to the far corners of the Earth and unearth ancient horrors in this Lovecraftian narrative puzzle adventure and sequel to 2020’s critically acclaimed Call of the Sea.

Roadside Research is a 1 to 4 player co-op gas station simulator. Except you’re aliens. And undercover. Do very human things like restocking shelves while preparing for the invasion. Just don’t get caught.

You can build (or neglect) the romance and relationship between Jason and Lucia in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Romance in GTA 6 isn't something you should shy away from. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as the pair reunite in Leonida. Whether they stick to being partners in crime or develop a healthy relationship status in GTA 6 is completely up-to you, with the connection between the two playable characters strengthening or weakening depending on your approach to the world. Jason and Lucia's relationship status isn't determined by completing certain missions or ticking off a few optional objectives, but rather it can change based on your actions, choices, and the time you spend together. Small acts of everyday affection and kindness will grow a healthier relationship in GTA 6, while ignoring your partner will slowly drive them apart.

There are four relationship statuses in GTA 6. You can move between each status at any time, organically depending on how you choose to play. You can track Jason and Lucia's relationship status at any time by holding right on the d-pad or by heading into the Jason & Lucia menu. They are (from least to most):

Tip: Jason and Lucia will remain connected as criminal partners throughout all of the GTA 6 missions, regardless of how their romantic relationship develops. However, certain moments in the story and interactions with characters may change depending on their relationship status at the time.

The process of building up your GTA 6 relationship status is organic – it happens gradually, over time through daily acts of affection and small acts of kindness. It's the smallest things that can make a difference, like greeting your partner when you meet up, buying them a snack, restocking their ammunition at an Ammu-Nation, or by holding hands while you explore the city together.

The bond between Jason and Lucia can also improve if you take time to do different activities together. Completing robberies and hitting gang hideouts together will strengthen their relationship, as will doing workouts together at the gym, and enjoying sports and leisure activities as a couple.

A little heart icon will appear on the screen beneath your health bar if you do something that your partner appreciates. Here's just a few examples of ways to improve your relationship status in GTA 6:

Tip: There are loads of ways to interact with your partner and collaborate in the world, more of which we detail in our guide to switching characters in GTA 6.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

To have the strongest relationship in GTA 6, both Jason and Lucia need to contribute to it. You can switch characters by holding right on the d-pad and then pressing R1. If you prioritize playing as one character over the other while you're playing, don't be surprised if the relationship naturally begins to degrade – this will impact the story and interactions between the two in a myriad of ways.

If you'd like to take more deliberate actions to lower your relationship status in GTA 6, then you certainly can do so. If you start ignoring your partner's calls and messages, don't be surprised if they start getting a little short with you on WhatUp. Spending lots of time apart, abandoning your partner while traveling together, or otherwise failing to engage with them on a daily basis will drive the two apart.

Tip: Small acts of affection will always help to improve the bond between Jason and Lucia, but if one of them has a GTA 6 Criminal Profile of 'Irredeemable' the relationship may never recover.

No, you cannot romance other characters beyond Lucia and Jason, at least through my experiences. I played through GTA 6 for over 100 hours and have yet to encounter any real opportunity to form a relationship or romance with any characters beyond those two, suggesting that their relationship is not an open one.

#3896. Monster Hunter Wilds' upcoming Ascendance expansion may be getting a beta, some curious Steam backend updates suggest

Monster Hunter Wilds's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year. But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the new stuff earlier than we thought.

On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer), which also shows an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance.

The beta app is the same one those who played the original Wilds beta had in their library. Though the app was removed following the beta's conclusion, because the two share the same ID, the beta should be visible in users' list of played games under the new name. This could mean players won't need to sign up for the supposed Ascendance beta, seemingly only needing to download the new client.

Seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement.

Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's new features. A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra, which we can hunt in the expansion.

Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty. While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge, Ascendance looks to be the next step up.

Three screens will show you more of Avengers: Doomsday

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Avengers: Doomsday is coming to the three-screen sensory overload that is ScreenX, with directors Anthony and Joe Russo promising a more complete look at the upcoming Marvel movie in the format.

"Avengers: Doomsday is massive," Anthony Russo began in a video from ScreenX. "From the beginning, we wanted audiences to experience the scale of this movie in the most impressive ways."

Joe Russo added, "We worked closely with the ScreenX team to design a version of the film specifically for this format, expanding the world of Doomsday beyond the main screen."

Then, Anthony Russo revealed ScreenX's unique selling point for fans who are aiming to be Avengers: Doomsday completionists: "You'll see things in ScreenX you simply will not see anywhere else."

As per Cineworld, the 12-projector setup of ScreenX is a "state-of-the-art atmospheric experience [that] surrounds you in your seat with innovative 270° projection across 3 screens, blended into 1 unforgettable projection experience."

Avengers: Doomsday will be available in multiple formats, including Marvel's own InfinityVision. IMAX screeners are expected to be available in early 2027 – thanks to Dune 3's exclusivity over the format.

Expect to see some intense thrills up on the big screen, too. The confirmed Avengers: Doomsday age rating has it locked in at PG-13 but, for the first time ever in an Avengers movie, will include "bloody images."

Avengers: Doomsday sees Fantastic Four, Fox's X-Men, and the MCU's Avengers team up to stop the twin threats of universe-ending incursions and the emergence of Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. With Hulk and Scarlet Witch seemingly already by his side, we might need those extra screens to see the sheer amount of Avengers who will be needed to stop this almighty threat.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and worldwide on December 18.

#3894. World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunters have found the MMO's first hidden treasure

World of Warcraft secret hunters are a noble breed, known for scouring the MMO for years for hidden trinkets and treasures. With World of Warcraft: Forever's launch, they've uncovered a quest chain for an especially fancy sword.

Over the past week, members of the WoW Secret Hunters Discord found a quest chain that takes place entirely on the Zephras Isle, meaning you'll need to have access to the Skyborne elves to grab this sword. Navigating the island, you'll need to first pick up an ancient heirloom ring from the starting zone. Simple enough!

Then, you'll need to head to Duskwood to gather the Night Watchman's Torch, a handy light source primarily used to light up areas across the darkened woods near Stormwind. It turns out this torch has uses far beyond this one zone however, as taking it back to the Ruins of Ban'aethal on the Zephras Isle will reward you with a secret quest and the Ancient Hilt.

With the hilt and ring, you then must track down an Ancient Blade from one of several spawn locations on the Zephras Isle. Once you finally track it down, that's the end of part one of this quest chain. You get the sword: Eluvi'ana, which on its own isn't particularly strong, but is speculated to be upgraded later down the line.

You then need to get a corrupted water globe from either Darkshore or the Blackfathom Deeps dungeon depending on your faction, do a fetch quest for a hidden spirit in Ashenvale, then take your hoard of special quest items to a NPC in the new Shen'Dralar zone.

He won't give you the finished sword. Instead he sends you to gather more items from higher-level zones. You'll need to raid a secluded vault in Feralas that you can only see with the Ancient Hilt, dive underwater in Azshara, and kill Highborne Shades in Winterspring. Once you've done all that, you can then cleanse the orb up in Hyjal, speak to the fella back in Shen'Dralar, then shimmy over to the end game Dire Maul dungeon to speak to Prince Tortheldrin about *another* sword.

This is how far the World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunter community has gotten to. It's believed that grinding up the Shen'dralar reputation to Honoured is required for the next step, as Prince Tortheldrin pretty much says as much in his dialogue. So the hunt is still on!

These sorts of secrets make up an important part of any good MMO: the solving of mysteries in these vast digital open worlds. In retail WoW, I have fond memories of the Waist of Time quest chain, which was an arduous and comical grind for a fancy belt during the Battle for Azeroth expansion. This secret sword quest chain may very well evolve into something as legendary as that, at least I hope so!

If you're not already playing it, World of Warcraft: Forever is plenty of fun. A record-breaking number of players are making the journey through Azeroth right now, diving into quests and dungeons new and old.

#3893. Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Currently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw quickly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is launched over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

The worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

#3892. GTA 6 Requires New PS5 Firmware Update to Play

As we reported early yesterday, PS5 has a new firmware update, numbered v14.23.00. It’s now confirmed you’ll need to have this installed to play GTA 6.

Notifying players on social media, a PlayStation Support page said: “Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing GTA 6. Players should download this update prior to midnight on 19th November so that they’re ready to play on launch day, 19th November.”

Sony usually gives users a period of grace to play their games before a new firmware update is made mandatory, so this is unprecedented behaviour.

But the stakes have never been higher either: Rockstar’s open world is the most anticipated game of all time, and it’s coming at a time when the PS5 has been cracked wide open.

Sony’s currently in a cat-and-mouse battle with hackers, as it tries to shore up the security of its console.

That all comes at the cost of inconvenience to the rest of us, as we’re forced to install firmware updates which have been coming more and more frequently of late.

This latest version is just 1.3GB so it’s not a huge lift, but this is your 24 hour warning that you’ll need to have it installed to play GTA 6.

#3891. Xbox Unveils New Halo Background & Default 'Event' Background For GTA 6

If you've turned on your Xbox console today and been presented with a background for GTA 6 without selecting it, there's a reason for that. Xbox is promoting the game by making a default "event" background for certain people.

You can let it sit there and do its thing if you want (although unfortunately it's not dynamic), or you can turn it off by going to Settings, Personalisation, My Background and then unticking the "show event-themed backgrounds" box.

In addition to this, Xbox has added a brand-new dynamic background for Halo: Campaign Evolved today, and it actually looks really, really cool. I might be rocking this background for a while to be honest!

Those who haven't been keeping track might also notice an Xbox 25 dynamic background that serves to celebrate Xbox's 25th anniversary. You'll find all of these by going to Settings, Personalisation, My Background and then browsing through the Dynamic Backgrounds that are on offer.

We'll leave you with a look at the Halo: Campaign Evolved background down below.
