The additional content you unlock through pre-ordering GTA 6 or buying the Ultimate Edition is all found in different locations

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Are you wondering how to unlock the GTA 6 pre-order and GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonuses? Don't worry, I was too through my first few hours in Leonida. It turns out that Rockstar Games doesn't want you having too many cool things too quickly, which is why you'll need to progress through different sections of the game before you'll gain access to unique weapons, vehicles, mod shops, clothing stores, and more that come as part of the DLC package, no matter which of the GTA 6 versions you own.

Below you'll find a breakdown of where to get the GTA 6 pre-order bonuses for both the Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition of the game. You'll also find a detailed breakdown of where to access all of the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition exclusives, which unlock as you progress through the story.

Regardless of whether you pre-ordered the Standard Edition or the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, you'll get access to a couple of nice bonus items. These are available from Chapter 3 onwards, and can be unlocked by doing the following:

The option to collect a uniquely-styled '55 Vapid Stainer vehicle from Vice Beach will appear as a task within the Exploration section of the map index. Once you've collected the vehicle from outside the Ocean View Hotel, you'll also unlock the Bonita Court Garage north of Washington Beach to store it in.

Once you've collected your '55 Vapid Stainer vehicle, you'll unlock some other bonuses as well. Head back to your residence and access the wardrobe to find exclusive outfits, and then visit any Salon to access a new hairstyle for Jason and Lucia under the Special section of the in-store menu.

As soon as you've found the 55 Vapid Stainer, the first thing you'll want to do is drive across to any Ammu-Nation store. Once inside, access the weapons locker and head into the Cosmetics / Wraps section of the modify menu on any gun to freely apply the pre-order exclusive weapon pattern.

If you purchase the more expensive GTA 6 Ultimate Edition, you'll find that Rockstar has well and truly made it worth your while. The exclusive storefronts, weapons, clothes, and vehicles aren't immediately accessible, instead they become available once you reach certain GTA 6 mission milestones:

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Once you're able to leave Jason's House in Chapter 1, you'll find two exclusive vehicles waiting for you. Underneath the house you'll find an Army fatigue-tinged Dinka Enduro motorcycle in the driveway, and off to the back of the building you'll spot a Crest Kayak which can be used to explore the Leonida Keys.

Only available for use in Chapter 1, you can get an exclusive pro build for Jason's Vapid Ganado pickup truck. Open up the map and head into the Vehicles index, from there click the Mod Shops option and look for Coastal Auto Care in Key Lento. Drive the Vapid Ganado over there and the unlock can be applied inside the Pro Builds / Full Kits section of the mod shop menu.

Take Jason to any Ammu-Nation store from Chapter 1 and access the weapon locker to unlock a personalized Girardi ES9 pistol. You can do the same with Lucia from Chapter 2 onwards, unlocking a unique Klose K17 pistol. Both of these weapons are free to equip and use.

Once you're into Chapter 2 of GTA 6, you'll be able to access unique weapon variants of the powerful Morgan revolver (regardless of whether you've already purchased the weapon). Jason and Lucia have their own versions, which can be accessed from any Ammu-Nation weapon locker.

Located in North Leonard County, just north of Lake Leonida, you'll gain access to One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop from Chapter 1. This GTA 6 Mod Shop specializes in off-road vehicles, and will give you access to a range of custom, hand-painted liveries for purchase.

Spend enough time meeting the locals at the Motel safehouse and you'll eventually meet Wyman, who will invite Lucia to the Thrillbilly Mud Club. Once you've completed a Dirt Track Race, look for a task in the exploration section of the map index to go collect your Dominator buggy and storage garage.

Once you have collected the Dominator buggy in Chapter 2, Wyman will contact you on WhatUp and ask for your help tracking down parts for classic cars. Look for the Find Cars for Wyman option in the exploration section of the map index to start this optional activity.

If you've got money to burn, then you'll want to take your favorite car over to Rideout Customs, located in the Crosstown district of Vice City. This Mod Shop offers unique interiors, rims, and stylings for any Donks vehicle classes. Head to the Vehicles map index and click the Mod Shops tab to set a destination.

Technically accessible from Chapter 1, there's a number of PTT YOUNGIN$ Compounds to raid for cash and key valuables. You'll need to head into Southside (south of Vice Dale County) to unlock these Illegal Operations. Once you've visited the area, head to the Robberies section of the map index.

Stock 305 can be found in the north quadrant of Vice City, in the Stockyard district. This skate store, selling contemporary streetwear and accessories, can be easily located by opening the map, heading to the style section of the index, and clicking onto the Casual & Street tab to get a destination.

Undoubtedly one of the better Hair & Beauty locations in GTA 6, Sara's Unisex Salon is located on the main strip of the Hamlet town. Find it in the Style section of map index. Once you're into Chapter 2, you'll gain access to exclusive signature looks for Jason and Lucia.

Located in the Stockyard area of Vice City, the Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor is open for business from Chapter 1. This tattoo parlor has over 50 signature tattoos for Jason and Lucia, all designed by the artist collective FAILE. Head to the Style section of the map index and look for the Tattoos tab.

The Wonder Whale is a Souvenir & Swimwear shop available for all players, located in the heart of the Key Leonto area (just off the main strip of highway). Head to the mannequins in the store to find some exclusive merch to purchase and wear. Just head to the Style section of the map index to get a location.

Once you're in Chapter 4, you've likely figured out the styles of both Jason and Lucia. Expect that to be challenged once a set of outfits are unlocked, for free – accessed directly from your wardrobe. A new set of tattoos are also available from most tattoo parlors, and new hair/beard styles at Sara's Unisex Salon.

Chapter 4 will also unlock a Shitzu Squalo for you to use for fishing and to search for dive sites in GTA 6. The boat is docked in a canal, south of the Washington Beach area of the map – just to the left of the Y Hotel. You can locate this vehicle at all times by heading to the Personal section of the map index.

An exclusive variant of one of the best cars in GTA 6 will be made available to you in Chapter 5. The '95 Grotti Cheetah is parked up in the garage beneath the Pegassi Residences building just waiting for you to collect it. You can also find a task in the Exploration section of the map index to help locate it.

#3889. As The Elder Scrolls 5 turns 15, massive mod Beyond Skyrim: Bruma gets a 2.0 update delivering a new quest, extra dungeons and an "expanded worldspace"

"The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity"

Warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 update to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are new quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

"You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding new content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 update. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

"The reason for this update is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

As laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several new dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

More clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A new opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

"All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

You can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's update.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a new playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

#3888. As of this week, PlayStation 5 has surpassed 100 million consoles sold

PlayStation 5 has officially surpassed 100m consoles sold, Sony's updated sales data revealed. The milestone was reached on 10th November, almost exactly six years on from the console's launch.

The figure represents 'sell-in' units, meaning those shipped to retailers, as opposed to 'sell-through' which tracks consoles actually sold to consumers. In other words, the number of PS5s in people's homes is smaller than that 100m.

Nevertheless, this is an impressive achievement, and gets the PS5 ever closer to the PS4's 117m, which it achieved by June 2022. It also means the PS5 has almost matched the original PlayStation in units sold (102.4m). As impressive as the numbers are, historical data shows that PS5 sales have been in decline.

Sony hasn't shied away from discussing that fact in its earnings reports. 2.6m PS5 consoles were sold during the most recent quarter (Q2 of FY2026), well below the 4m sold over the same period the year prior. In fact, Q2 of FY2026 is the lowest second quarter on record in terms of units sold since the PS5's launch.

However, it's also worth noting that, small though it may be, the second quarter's result is higher than the first quarter's 1.6m, the second-lowest of any single quarter since the PS5's launch, beaten only by Q4 of FY2025's 1.5m.

If numbers don't recover in the third and fourth quarters, this may be the PS5's lowest year ever in terms of units sold. Although the second quarter's sales boost can be attributed to the high anticipation of Grand Theft Auto 6, the overall downturn is largely due to the console's higher price; Sony raised the PS5 and PS5 Pro's prices on several occasions since 2020. The company's bottom line, however, hasn't been affected much, as its plan to generate more revenue from its already-engaged audience continues to work.

"Yes," indeed, a Blade Runner game might be underway

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Blade Runner 2099 isn't here just yet, with Amazon Prime's new take on the iconic cinematic cyberpunk universe set to arrive on November 25 – but its producers are already discussing a potential video game, apparently.

News of the possible game comes directly from IGN, who learns from Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson – Blade Runner 2099 executive producers and co-CEOs of Blade Runner franchise owner Alcon Entertainment – that, "yes," it might be underway somewhere down the line. And, furthermore, the two emphasize that it'll be a "AAA" project if anything, meaning this won't be a small fish situation… It may be the Blade Runner game.

Although Kosove and Johnson couldn't give much more information on the mysterious (possible, as it seems now) game, they do stress how important allowing players "interact" with the cyberpunk universe will be. It is, after all, a level of immersion Blade Runner's not really featured before, despite having been in the limelight in some shape or form since its 1982 debut film – the Ridley Scott classic that started it all.

I do wonder what the Blade Runner game might look like, should it come to fruition, though. Will it be akin to Cyberpunk 2077 – an RPG that leans heavily on player choice but builds its own universe with unique characters, standing comfortably separate from its tabletop source material – or shall it feature faces familiar to longtime fans (perhaps even those introduced in Blade Runner 2099 next week)? Only time will tell.

Regardless, it's an exciting time to be a fan of the gritty, sci-fi cyberpunk genre, if you ask me. Between CD Projekt Red's own confirmed Cyberpunk 2 and now a potential Blade Runner game, there's plenty for players to anticipate.

#3886. The Outer Worlds 2's first story expansion could well be the opening to the series' last hurrah and will have you hunting for a cure to "explosive cell death" in December

Sub Rosa sci-fi drama and a new region to explore await

Since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a new Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC plans. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That said, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game currently looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:

As you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

Rounding out the expansion are new enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an update alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

As much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.

#3885. "I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released" - former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada trashes Microsoft's console in front of senior Xbox staff

Katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches. This truth was reinforced recently, as he said he wished the Xbox Series S "wouldn't be released" at a developer panel. All while a member of the Xbox team was in the room.

Per Inven Global, Harada was sitting on a panel at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea. The panel was moderated by former Sony president Shuhei Yoshida, and featured Shift Up CTO DongKi Lee (Stellar Blade), Too Kyo Games CEO Kazutaka Kodaka (Dangenrompa), CD Projekt Red associate game director Paweł Sasko (Cyberpunk 2077), Ludeon Studios CEO Tynan Sylvester (Rimworld), and of course CEO of the newly formed VS Studio Katsuhiro Harada (Tekken).

The panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms. Harada led the charge, speaking to the advantages consoles provide for fighting game developers, as the hardware is ideal for tournaments and esports events. Following this, he took an opportunity to speak about a console that drew his ire.

"That said, there's something I really want to say while I have the floor. Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released," Harada said (translations to English via Inven Global). Harada then asked Sasko from the CD Projekt Red team whether he was "upset inside" because of the Xbox Series S.

Sasko proceeded to "burst out laughing" according to Inven Global, before responding: "It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly."

Harada followed up with additional thoughts: "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say "Xbox Series S sucks," right? (laughs) Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to 'Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!' But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child.

"Furthermore, in markets like the US, there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking 'Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'"

Sasko stepped up to offer some perks to the Series S. While he agreed that many players the full technical context behind the Series S' weaknesses, he pointed out that optimisation for weaker hardware like the Series S made games run "significantly better" across all platforms. He even had a Cyberpunk 2077 example, as optimisation work done for the Switch 2 version were applied to all platforms "to great effect". Sasko also pointed to the affordability side of the argument, saying that the cheaper price of the Series S allows for market expansion.

Harada responded: "Director Paweł packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I'm worried they'll feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs)."

Here, Shift Up's DongKi Lee ended the topic with some optimism for Microsoft's future consoles: "Personally, I am looking forward to the next-gen Xbox 'Helix'. From an engineer's standpoint, if you provide us with a dev kit first in Korea as early as possible, we will put in our best efforts to develop for it."

Earlier this year Harada founded Vs Studio with SNK's support, with other veterans from Bandai Namco's Tekken team hopping on board for whatever it's working on. As for the Xbox Helix consoles, in this current hardware environment with bloated costs for RAM and other components, it's reportedly looking a tad expensive. Maybe a Series S equivalent is on the cards?

#3884. Review: GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

What does eight years and an estimated $1 billion get you? Well, GTA 6.

In this long-anticipated crime sandbox, Rockstar has assembled the most technologically accomplished open world ever made, expanding on its groundbreaking work with Red Dead Redemption 2.

But crucially, with its dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, it’s grown up a bit.

This is the franchise at its most mature, shedding the cartoonish cultural caricatures of GTA 5 without losing the biting social commentary the series is known for.

The fictional state of Leonida is undoubtedly the star here; a dense and gigantic urban sandbox populated by an unfathomable array of art assets.

Whether it’s the easy-living coastal island of Key Lento or the mean streets of Crosstown, Rockstar’s artistry is utterly unprecedented.

Zoom in and you’ll see insects attracted to discarded food wrappers; a single convenience store has more unique art assets than entire districts in other open world games. This is remarkable stuff, delivered at such a scale it’s going to leave other publishers with their heads in their hands.

It feels alive, too; a casual visit to a gas station saw me berated by a cyclist for my wayward driving (I told him to chill out), while a brief pause on the side-walk ended up with my car getting hijacked by a masked criminal.

In over 150 hours of play, I’m still discovering random events that add depth and character to the open world. And even when the scripting is pushed to the background, the way every NPC feels designed, with distinctive personality and unique body types, makes this package an unfathomable feat.

But while Leonida is the standout, Jason and Lucia are the vehicles that guide you through it.

Just like GTA 5, each character has their own individual life, but the game is at its best when it brings them together.

I’ve never seen romance made into a mechanic quite like this, aside from perhaps the handholding in ICO, which is repurposed here. (Complete with DualSense haptic feedback when the characters touch.)

Jason is a bit of a beige blank slate, but Lucia brings genuine “girl power” to the story without pandering or feeling insincere.

In fact, in contrast to past GTAs, the many women in this instalment feel much more believable; the game frequently flips expectations on their head, without it ever coming across as forced.

A secret twist revealed in the opening moments adds gravity to the couple’s situation and becomes the driving force behind the story, which takes the pair from pillar to post, fulfilling the whims of a ragtag roster of ne’er-do-wells.

The campaign does fall into cliche territory at times, as the pair bounce from one bad idea to another in order to fulfil their ultimate ambition, and it’s something the characters seem to acknowledge. (“When are we going to get to call our own shots?” Jason wearily ponders at one point.)

But the mission design remains inventive throughout, regularly adding bespoke mechanics and interactions to keep things fresh.

In one early mission, Jason indulges his inner-PowerWash Simulator, as he rinses down a boat while other characters commentate key plot points. I won’t spoil the best moments, but needless to say there are missions here that will be remembered for a long time.

There’s also a slate of optional pastimes running concurrently to the main campaign which add genuine variety to the sandbox.

I was most enamoured by Jason’s home entertainment setup, which includes a distinctly PS4 coded console that can be powered up. I’ll leave you to discover his selection of fully playable games.

But beyond that, the ability to go hunting or even play a round of golf means you can lose yourself in this sandbox for hours at a time, and never really tire of the activities available to you.

Some of the action sequences remind me of all-time classics like Uncharted 3 – fist-pumping, set-piece heavy rollercoaster rides that push Rockstar’s engine to its limits, all within the confines of a meticulously designed open world.

Controller response is vastly superior to the studio’s previous games, with the cover shooting system feeling much more natural and the aiming mechanics buoyed by a pretty fun “bullet time” mechanic.

However, the game does fall into the trap of introducing heavily armoured bullet sponge enemies towards its conclusion, as it runs out of ways to make human-on-human encounters interesting.

That said, I really appreciated the agency GTA 6 gives you over how you approach each situation; non-vitals can be targeted to incapacitate enemies without murdering them, while it’s perfectly possible to sneak in and out of many areas without ever being detected.

This all builds a criminal profile which changes how the police and wider world will interact with you. Meanwhile, you can influence Jason and Lucia’s relationship itself, opting to keep them close or distant depending on how you want things to play out.

An early optional objective allows you to decorate Jason’s idyllic beach house in anticipation of Lucia’s arrival. Complete it in time and the couple will grow closer; ignore it and she’ll acknowledge you didn’t go the extra mile.

Other interactions are subtler: a kiss and cuddle on the balcony of the pair’s Vice City penthouse will strengthen their bond, but it’s up to you whether you want to invest in their relationship or not.

Multiple endings mean there are actual consequences to your actions, even if some decisions along the way feel more like an illusion than something truly meaningful.

The plot does begin to drag in its latter phases, and I do think Rockstar could have tightened up the roughly 60 hour storyline, which will likely take the average player around 80 hours to complete when accounting for the vast amount of side content as well.

(A 100% save could take anywhere up to 300 hours or more, depending on how much support you get from guides.)

As a crime sandbox, I also wanted to mention the ‘Wanted’ system, which has come on leaps and bounds.

A coordinated robbery can be accomplished without ever triggering a traditional car chase, as the game accounts for your outfit, vehicle, weapons, and much more.

Successfully scouting out your targets, and planning accordingly with a change of clothes and getaway car, can see you slip past the police undetected. Few moments in gaming are more satisfying than when you casually drive past a fleet of incoming cop cars, with a bag of successfully looted narcotics in your trunk.

Some players may respond negatively to the life sim elements here, which reward you for exercising and require you to occasionally put gas in your car or eat something.

But I think it adds to the immersive nature of the open world, and concessions have been made to the realism when it makes sense; a quick request to Scooter Bros, for example, will see your favourite car instantaneously delivered to your current location, so you don’t have to wait around.

The biggest downside to the outright awesome spectacle of the open world is that it runs at 30fps on the PS5 Pro, with no option to double the frame rate or tailor the presentation to taste, as has become standard in most other games.

Objectively this is disappointing, but given the sheer scale of Leonida I think it’s a necessary compromise.

It should be noted that despite all this, the frame pacing is solid and the game feels smooth and responsive as a result. I encountered very few (if any) instances of slowdown – even when flying over the map in a jet or speeding down highways being chased by rival gangs.

The audio presentation matches the high standards of the visuals, with different engine growls depending on how you’ve modified your vehicle. (Midnight Club fans may be excited to learn the racing missions here rival most dedicated franchises like Need for Speed alone.)

There are multiple fist-pumping audio cues, which leverage the title’s enormous licensed soundtrack to excellent effect. But credit must also go to composer duo Justice, who bring their distinct brand of disco-inspired electronica to the soundscape, elevating some of the best missions to impressive highs.

And I was blown away by how much texture the DualSense adds, with one of my favourite features being the feedback you feel when you pass cars at speed on the highway. The only thing I didn’t like was the use of adaptive triggers, which feel far too stiff and lack the nuance of first-party games.

Guide GTA 6 Guide: All Guides & Collectibles

GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.

Crucially, despite the 30fps cap, the gameplay feels responsive and you have much more authorship over how you want to approach it. I enjoyed preparing for my robberies and feeling like I was rewarded for the legwork.

The audiovisual presentation is a new high for the industry, with a frankly flabbergasting array of art assets bringing it all to life.

But I think Jason and Lucia’s ragtag romance, which is central to everything in the game, also demonstrates an unexpected maturity – without completely removing the silly sense of downright dumb humour the series is known for.

Despite unprecedented expectations, GTA 6 delivers – and then some.

He’s an expert on PS Studios and industry matters, as well as sports games and simulators. He also enjoys RPGs when he has the time to dedicate to them, and is a bit of a gacha whale.

#3883. Three Major New Games Have Added Free Xbox Trials And Demos

We don't tend to highlight demos and trials on the Xbox Store all that often, but when you get multiple recent releases (some of them AAA) suddenly getting freebies, they definitely can't go unmentioned!

The three games we're talking about in particular here are Control Resonant, Crimson Desert Enhanced and Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival. The first two have free trials (and we actually mentioned the Crimson Desert one in a separate article back in October), while Hellraiser: Revival has a free new demo.

You can access free trials by going to the game's official Xbox Store page and then hitting the "Free Trial" button, which will typically download the entire game and give you access to just a couple of hours of it. Demos, meanwhile, are separate downloads that are hidden away in the "Demos" section of the Xbox Store.

There are some other recently-added demos as well if you're interested - here are all the "New" examples:

Control Resonant is probably the one that everyone's going to focus on here, as it literally only came out in late September and already has a way to try it for free. That's amazing news for anyone who might have been on the fence.

Don't sleep on the others as well though, especially considering how the "Enhanced" version of Crimson Desert refers to the updated August 2026 version rather than the one that first released in March, while Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival has been getting "Very Positive" feedback on Steam and is only a few weeks old!

We'll leave you with more details on all the three main games below:

Play through the Prologue, where Aidan follows Sunny into the Labyrinth and discovers a terrifying, ever-shifting realm of nightmares. Then, experience a portion of Episode 1, where Aidan must escape the clutches of the Scarlet Church, who have taken the Genesis Configuration into their possession.

Join Dylan in this sequel to the multi-award-winning CONTROL to explore the expansive zones of a city overrun by the corrupting influences of the chaotic Hiss, invasive micro-organism, the Mold, and other twisted paranatural threats.

Discover an enhanced Crimson Desert, featuring new cutscenes and story moments, plus expanded voice-over and language support. ​ Begin the adventure loved by millions, refined since launch with a wealth of updates, including new content, mounts, pets, customization options, various quality-of-life improvements, and more. ​

Nintendo launches its official Black Friday Switch 2 deals this Sunday, November 22. But that doesn't mean there isn't already a wealth of discounts on the shelves. While things are a little slower in this department compared to PS5 (Sony dropped its own offers earlier this week), retailers like Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and GameStop have all launched their own early discounts and we're truly in the swing of sales now.

The big ticket we're waiting for is that Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle. It's the go-to for anyone upgrading their handheld this Black Friday, packing a free copy of the latest racer as well as a Nintendo Switch Online Individual subscription. Considering the game itself usually piles an additional $79.99 onto your cart, that's a Black Friday deal to wait for.

You'll also be waiting until Sunday for $20 discounts on games like Donkey Kong Bananza and Kirby Air Riders, but plenty of third party titles or games not yet mentioned in Nintendo's upcoming Black Friday Switch 2 deals are already at their lowest prices yet. Ocarina of Time Remake, for example, has only just sailed down to its cheapest $54.99 rate this week, and you'll still find Mario Kart World on sale at Walmart by itself as well.

I've counted up 15 of the best Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals you can already get your hands on before Ninty's sale has even begun - and you'll find them all just below.

I've spent more than seven years tracking Black Friday deals, but I watch prices on top games and gadgets all year round. I was with the Switch 2 from day one, completing GamesRadar+'s review of the latest generation handheld and going hands-on with as many accessories and titles as possible since. That means I know which prices actually represent discounts on the tech you actually need to know about.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is seeing a rare discount at Woot right now, with $30 off a new device. Savings here are usually limited to refurbished models so, while we're still above the previous $449 MSRP (prices jumped to $499 in November) this is one of the few discounts we've seen in the last couple of months.

Switch Sports Resort is being bundled in with the Nintendo Switch 2 console for just $30 extra right now. With the new $499 MSRP of the handheld and the latest island mini game pack coming in at $59.99, that's a solid saving.

This is Nintendo's Black Friday showpiece. The Mario Kart World bundle will be dropping to $499.99 from November 22, essentially netting you the $79.99 racer for free. That's with a Nintendo Switch Online Individual subscription thrown in as well.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has seen discounts in its life before, but only during its pre-order phase. That was when the physical edition dropped from $69.99 to $59.99. Today, the digital edition is giving us a brand new record-low price on 2026's biggest Ninty release.

Read more: Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time remake review

High on Life 2 is down to its lowest price yet in Amazon's Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals. The FPS made its way to Ninty's handheld this year, but has been stuck at full price until July. Since then, it's only been on sale for about $40, before dropping down to today's $29.99 position.

So long as you don't mind adding a game-key card to your collection, Persona 3 Reload is down to just $25 right now ahead of Black Friday. This is a brand new record-low price on the Switch 2 version.

Mouse: PI for Hire is seeing its first ever discount right now, so while it may be small anyone waiting for a saving on this detective noir adventure should be taking notes. It's just started to move down the price scale to $34.99, so good things could be on their way.

Here's how this deal works. The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild will cost you $69 on Switch 2 if you buy the physical copy. An upgrade from the Switch 1 version, however, will only set you back $9.99. Take Woot's current $46.99 sale price on the original cart, add that upgrade price, and you've got the full Switch 2 experience for just $56.98 (about $12 off).

Read more: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild review

Metroid Ravenous is seeing the same pattern a number of first party Switch 2 pre-orders have seen this year - a $10 discount at Amazon that disappears after release. This is a solid chance to save ahead of that January launch date.

We've only ever seen Pokemon Scarlet drop to $45 once in the many years since its original release date. So, while this is an older Switch title, it runs great on Switch 2 and this is definitely a rare discount if you've not played it yet.

Mario Kart World still retails for essentially full price, which was $79 on launch day. Seeing any kind of discount on this racer is pretty rare, but Walmart's early Black Friday deals have it down to $68.40 now.

Donkey Kong Bananza will be $49.99 when Nintendo unleashes its full Black Friday sale on November 22. That will represent a record-low on the rarely discounted bananza smasher.

Kirby Air Riders will drop down to $39.99 on November 22, another record-low for a game that's seen a little more wiggle room on its price tag compared to Donkey Kong. Air Riders has shifted between $50 and $60 for a few months now, but it's never dropped this cheap.

Metroid Prime 4 will be another Switch 2 game joining the $39.99 club this Black Friday. We're already half way there at Amazon, but it's worth holding off on this one until November 22.

It may be an OG Switch port of two far older games, but the Super Mario Galaxy collection doesn't see too many discounts day to day. This one's only dropped to a similar $48.97 position once before Black Friday, back in September.

The Switch 2 version of Super Mario Party Jamboree is actually one of the most expensive games on the system, but the full cart has dropped to this Black Friday's $59.99 price before. That was during a very brief flash sale back in March, though, otherwise this is an $80 title day to day.

The PowerA Slim Case is one of the cheaper clamshell options on the market, so its $19.99 MSRP doesn't have too far to drop. A 25% discount takes a solid $5 off the price here, within a few pennies of its lowest ever.

The Turtle Beach Airlite Fit is one of the cheapest headset options out there for the Switch 2 at full price, so a record-low $14.99 is going to be particularly handy for anyone looking for an easy wired set of cups.

Featured in: Best Nintendo Switch headset

Read more: Turtle Beach Airlite Fit review

A smaller saving on a cheaper Joy-Con replacement system here. The GameSir X5s doesn't hold up against some of the more luxurious options on the market, but if you want a wider set of gamepads for handheld mode it's looking far more affordable than official pads right now.

The GameSir Super Nova regularly tails it down to this $29.99 sales position, but that doesn't make it any less impressive. In the hands this feels far more premium than a $30 gamepad should. Considering we're at a record-low price and this is the rate I'd expect to see in official Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals, this is an easy win.

Featured in: Best Nintendo Switch 2 controllers

A golden oldie here, the Razer Barracuda X has been a go-to Switch headset for almost as long as it's been on the shelves, and it rarely drops below today's $69 sales position.

Black Friday itself officially kicks off on November 27, but Nintendo's offers come into full effect on November 22. That's for physical games and handhelds, though. Digital collectors are also being treated to an eShop sale running from November 19 until December 2.

We're also busy preparing for this year's best Black Friday PS5 deals and the best Black Friday gaming laptop deals as well.

#3881. Lootboxes, pay-to-win, virtual currencies and other blights unto gaming face heavy regulation as the EU tables new Digital Fairness Act

It's been 10 years since I lasted opened a lootbox, I think. Just thought you should know.

Loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today. The full draft text of the regulation leaked earlier in the week. If it passes into law - and there's plenty of debate and revision ahead - it'll have big consequences for the developers and publishers of games like Overwatch, Dota 2, and GTA Online.

You can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site. The organisers have also published an introductory explainer that takes us through the timeline of the Act's gestation, dating back to 2020, and summarises its provisions. If passed, the Act will apply to any company doing business in the EU, not just those based in member states, with individual governments able to impose fines and consumers able to seek financial compensation if they think they've been harmed.

Here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text. The Act proposes a number of provisions regarding "unfair" commercial practices, including omission and distortion in advertising and PR communication at large. Amongst other things, it takes aim at "dark patterns" – that is, "visual, auditory and other components" of online interfaces that are designed to manipulate or deceive. The text also forbids personalised advertising and pricing aimed at children, and prohibits influencers from making "direct exhortations to minors to buy products or to persuade their parents or other adults to buy products in commercial communications".

The items that are probably of greatest interest to us smelly gamers are the passages on virtual currencies, "variable reward systems", and addictive design.

The Act would require game publishers who sell virtual currencies to indicate the real-world monetary value of the currency and anything bought with it. It would also require companies to disable paid-for virtual currencies by default for kids, unless a parent or guardian has given approval.

As for paid-for "variable reward systems", aka "loot boxes", "surprise mechanics", "Schrödinger's Giftbombs" or however publishers may prefer to describe them, the Act would require companies to state the "types" of object they might cough up, together with the probability of obtaining them. It would also oblige publishers to disable paid-for "variable reward systems" for minors, and give everybody an "easily accessible" way to switch them off.

The draft Act outright prohibits "pay-to-progress and pay-to-win mechanisms" for kids. More generally, it suggests further constraints for publishers and developers who "design, organise or operate their digital products in a manner that is intended, or can reasonably be foreseen to encourage compulsive or excessive use". Again, it wants companies to give people options to switch these features off.

That includes "features enabling automatic play of content and uninterrupted content consumption without effective and regular interruption moments that enable deliberation by the consumer on their willingness to consume more content". Also, "notifications not triggered by, or not directly related to, the consumer’s interaction or activity on the service", "features incentivising engagement at regular times or with greater frequency, including through penalties or loss of benefits", and "features and system behaviours that encourage continued use by simulating interpersonal relations," such as nagging prompts.

If you'd like a more 'expert' account of the Digital Fairness Act - how dare you! I have read several Wikipedia pages - the bespectacled nabobs of GamesIndustry.biz went and got notes from an actual lawyer. All this follows a change in EU rating law last month aimed at safeguarding the weans from predatory habit-forming devices and instruments of financialisation - games with lootboxes are now PEGI 16 by default, while blockchain games are always rated 18. Across the pond, meanwhile, lawsuits are underway in New York and Washington against Valve's tolerance of lootboxes on Steam, which the lawyers in question define as illegal gambling.

#3880. Hell Let Loose's original developers' Napoleonic-era extraction game, Hunger, gets December early access release, and an open beta this month

Good Fun Corp, the studio made up of the original developers behind Hell Let Loose, has finally announced a release date for its anticipated next project: Hunger. The extraction shooter-slasher game enters early access on Steam on 3rd December, and there's good news if you're eager to try it out before then.

Hunger's first and only open beta has also been announced, taking place 27th-29th November, the weekend prior to its early access launch. Unlike past tests, this one is available for anyone who requests access on Steam.

Though it may appear as yet another extraction shooter on the surface, Hunger offers more complex and intertwined systems than most. For one, combat has a focus on melee with only a few intentionally clunky firearms available. Though this is a PvPvE game, the vs environment side includes the sort of puzzle-solving, questing and dungeon-raiding typical of RPGs. The game's alternate history, plague-ravaged European setting gives it a grimey, steel-and-mud look few games have.

Beyond the in-match experience, Good Fun's ambitions extend to Hunger's MMO-style progression, its hub area with distinct characters and varied playable classes - all of which can be sampled in the upcoming beta.

Hunger just came off a very successful closed beta, which clearly didn't suffer by kicking off right alongside Modern Warfare 4's DMZ early access. Hunger is currently among Steam's most-wishlisted games, with over 700,000 wishlists, according to the developer.

The launch version includes three large maps, six playable characters, and five Mastery trees with more than 100 Masteries to unlock for your characters. Hunger has only been announced for PC so far, but will presumably arrive on consoles following its early access journey.

#3878. "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty": Destroy All Humans! remake devs Black Forest Games split from THQ Nordic to launch new indie studio group

"We're excited to shape our own future as owners again"

Black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans! remakes, have spun out of Embracer Group-owned publishers THQ Nordic via a management buyout and announced plans to form a new "developer-driven group" of independent studios. The new group, dubbed Third Signal, will aim to "give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom" to "bring their own ideas to life".

Black Forest, based in Germany, announced the move in a press release. "We are grateful to THQ Nordic and Embracer for nine good years and the games we made together," co-boss Adrian Goersch said. "Now, we're excited to shape our own future as owners again, to work on an exciting new project with a great team and strong partners behind us."

Black Forest had been in the embrace since 2017, releasing both 2020's Destroy All Humans! remake and Destroy All Humans! 2: Reprobed in that time, plus DLC Clone Carnage. Over the years they've also made multiple entries in the Giana Sisters platformer series, survival game Fade to Silence, and 2017's Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back.

That's a right old mix of stuff, but the biggest names in it are all resurrections of series or characters created by other folks back in the day. Pandemic Studios in the case of Destroy All Humans!, Accolade in the case of Bubsy, and Germany company Time Warp in the case of Giana Sisters. That makes the fact it sounds like this move'll give Black Forest a bit more creative freedom intriguing. Here's hoping that if they do plan to try and get some more of their own original ideas off the ground, rather than trucking on with a steady diet of remakes and revivals, they manage to stick the landing. It's all fine declaring that a 50 person team can make a top game these days, but that certainly doesn't mean it's in any way easy to pull off.

#3877. 'PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough to Run GTA 6 at 60fps': Rockstar Explains Frame Rate Decision

I’ve played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro for over 150 hours and it’s a remarkable experience. You can read my review through here.

This is the densest open world ever designed. The sheer amount of art assets on screen at any given time is simply unprecedented.

There is a downside to all the detail, though: the Rockstar release bucks contemporary console trends and runs at 30fps, without compromise. There’s no Performance option, even on Sony’s most powerful platform, which will run you $900 these days.

I spoke to Rockstar’s Marc Chambers, the man in charge of Technology Production to try to understand why.

“The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the games visual fidelity,” he said.

“While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it’s not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”

In other words, it’s as many already predicted: GTA 6’s performance is limited by its robust CPU demands.

Chambers continued: “GTA 6 pushes the current-generation console hardware to its absolute limits. The complexity of simulating and rendering the environments and inhabitants in a world the scale of Leonida, while maintaining the density, visual fidelity, and player agency we envisaged, places extraordinary demands on the hardware. Bringing all of these systems together and completing the required work for every frame is only just possible within a ~33ms frame budget.”

The remarkable thing to me is, despite the drop to 30fps, I found the game to feel very responsive overall. Aiming is snappy and movement feels less cumbersome than in past Rockstar releases, like Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rockstar’s Vice President of Technology David Hynd told me that the team was able to remove one full frame of delay compared to past titles.

“The input controller is sampled as late as possible during the game update. As a consequence, the game is updated with the most recent input data and we minimise the time between pressing a button and seeing the results on screen,” he said.

You really do feel this: I was switching between GTA 6 and several other 60fps PS5 games during the review process, and while the frame rate difference was obvious to my eyes, it didn’t feel as dramatic as I’d expected.

“For our game mechanics, we ensured that we stripped as much ‘dead space’ out of the start of our animations as possible,” Hynd continued. “And ensured that we could seamlessly interrupt them as early as was practical.”

There are still moments where GTA 6 feels clumsy, but it’s a marked improvement in playability compared to past games, despite the drop in frame rate.

Overall, I think Rockstar made the right decision.

The decision to lock gameplay at 30fps is objectively disappointing, but on a PS5 Pro the performance is smooth throughout, and the controller response is surprisingly good.

With the sheer amount of art assets on the screen at any given time, I think it would have been a shame to see Rockstar compromise its vision.

This is the most immersive open world ever made, and I think it’s clear the team has put as much thought as possible into making sure it feels smooth and responsive at 30fps.

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

As the Editor of Push Square, Sammy has over 15 years of experience analysing the world of PlayStation, from PS3 through PS5 and everything in between. He’s an expert on PS Studios and industry matters, as well as sports games and simulators. He also enjoys RPGs when he has the time to dedicate to them, and is a bit of a gacha whale.

#3876. GTA 6 might be censored in Japan, if the game's smaller install size and lack of "strong sexual content" warning is anything to go by

GTA 6 is finally coming out worldwide next week, putting an end to a 13-year wait and at least one popular meme format, but the highly-anticipated game might look a bit different in Japan.

Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

The potential regional censorship isn't too surprising, though, considering how trimmed down GTA 5's Japanese release was at the time. Rockstar had to remove and alter a bunch of GTA 5 scenes to comply with the country's normally strict content guidelines, including Trevor's controversial torture segment and multiple scenes featuring nudity. Baldur's Gate 3, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and many more have been subject to similar restrictions in the past.

Earlier this week, GTA 6 became the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation and Xbox's history. That's also not a huge surprise, either. The juggernaut game's lavish marketing blitz took over London's Selfridges and Rockstar is even hosting an entire music festival starring a couple A-listers.

#3875. There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

Suddenly, making faster chips mattered less than a faster release schedule - and most of the industry couldn’t keep up

Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.

In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the new millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD.

But the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor. Research firm 4th Wave put ATI top for 1998 with 24.5 million 3D chips sold, followed by S3 with 15.2 million and Intel, in its first year in the market, with 6.5 million. Nvidia came fourth on 6.4 million. 3dfx, the company whose Voodoo cards had made 3D gaming on PC a thing in the first place, sold 5.2 million.

Each of those companies went under or sold up for one reason or another, but what’s striking is how most did so within a few years of one another. In the four years between 1998 and 2002, the graphics business essentially stopped rewarding whoever had the fastest chip, instead favouring the companies that could iterate the fastest. A new chip every six months or so for the same APIs everyone used, backed by enough capital to ride out the dot-com crash. Nvidia was built for that; almost nobody else was.

The first companies to go didn’t need any help from Nvidia, though. 3D acceleration had made the humble graphics chip a much bigger and more expensive thing to design, and plenty of incumbents that had found their footing on 2D couldn’t afford to keep going. Tseng Labs stopped developing graphics chips at the end of 1997 with roughly $28 million still in the bank, selling its graphics engineers to ATI for about $3 million. Rendition, maker of the Vérité V1000 3D accelerator, agreed to sell itself to memory maker Micron in June 1998, and ATI bought Chromatic Research for $67 million that October.

In its prospectus for its January 1999 IPO, Nvidia warned that PC makers brought out new systems as often as twice a year, on a spring and fall schedule, and that missing one was a serious risk. The company subsequently reorganised itself around that schedule, releasing the GeForce 256 in October 1999 and the GeForce 3 in February 2001. By 2002, Nvidia’s annual report disclosed that separate design teams were working on several generations of chips at once.

By this point, though, the writing had been on the wall for quite some time. S3, then the world’s second-largest graphics chip maker, wrote in its annual report for 1999 that a graphics chip stayed on sale for 12 to 18 months, and that a delay "as short as a few months" could cost it a design win with a PC maker. Any company that was rolling out just one major chip per year was launching against a rival’s refresh at best. At worst, it was launching late against next-gen chips.

That’s essentially what happened to 3dfx when Rampage, the chip that was meant to succeed the Voodoo5, never shipped. The company lost its other big advantage around the same time with Glide, its own programming interface that only ran on Voodoo cards. Glide flourished while Direct3D, Microsoft’s rival interface built into Windows, was still lacking features, meaning that plenty of games ran best on 3dfx hardware, but that lead was quickly eroded once Direct3D and rivals’ OpenGL drivers caught up; developers could now write a game once and run it on anyone’s card. By 1999, Creative was selling Nvidia-based Riva TNT cards with drivers that let Glide games run on them. 3dfx sued, then open-sourced Glide altogether that December.

By then, though, 3dfx had already made its most damaging mistake. A year earlier, on December 14, 1998, it agreed to buy graphics card maker STB Systems for about $141 million in stock, and CEO Greg Ballard said the Voodoo3 would only be sold on 3dfx’s cards. That revelation left Diamond and Creative in a tough spot, having built their gaming lines on Voodoo chips. They were now stuck high and dry without access to the new one.

3dfx was solely concerned with its margins here. The price of its single-chip Voodoo Banshee card dropped from $150 to $89 within a month of launch. With prices in freefall, selling the finished Voodoo Banshee meant that 3dfx pocketed the margin that’d otherwise go to a partner like Diamond or Creative. Those boardmakers inevitably walked, and went where the chips were. STB had been selling Nvidia cards right up to the deal, and its last annual report includes a $3 million note it held from "Nvidia Corporation, a supplier." Creative already had Riva TNT cards on shelves, and Nvidia, which then didn’t make its own cards, would sell its chips to anyone.

Intel, meanwhile, was causing problems from the other end of the market. Its i740 "Auburn" graphics chip launched in early 1998, and Microprocessor Report, the newsletter for the industry’s engineers, argued that Intel’s arrival encouraged Cirrus Logic, Oak and others to fold that year. Just over a year later, after lacklustre sales, Intel confirmed that it was ending support for the i740, then pulled out of standalone desktop graphics chips altogether to put graphics into its motherboard chipsets instead, starting with the i810. This was extremely problematic for companies like S3, Trident, and SiS. They survived on cheap chips for big PC makers, and by the second half of 2001, estimates say Intel’s integrated graphics business had risen to control 55% of the market. That, in turn, pushed S3 to sell its graphics business to a VIA joint venture for $323 million.

Then the money ran out. Venture funding for graphics startups had already dried up in 1999 as the dot-com bubble deflated, and exits inevitably followed. 3dfx lost $100.5 million in the second quarter of 2000, with its CEO blaming a late Voodoo5, and on December 15 that year it sold its assets to Nvidia for $70 million in cash (and a million Nvidia shares) after failing to secure credit. STMicroelectronics, which made the PowerVR-based Kyro II, quit PC graphics in early 2002.

ATI, however, survived alongside Nvidia because it was already operating in the way the new market wanted it to. It was the biggest seller at the time, and it made its own graphics cards, which Microprocessor Report said brought in most of its revenue and margin. So, making its own cards wasn’t 3dfx’s mistake; it was locking out boardmakers who had been selling Voodoo cards for it. That pushed those boardmakers towards Nvidia, and a late Voodoo5 and cash crunch dealt the death blow. ATI also used its stock to buy the engineers that its rivals were shedding: Tseng’s, Chromatic’s, then, in February 2000, ArtX’s for $400 million, a team that’d just designed the Flipper graphics chip for Nintendo’s GameCube.

For the next two decades, the the graphics industry was dominated by ATI - which eventually folded into AMD in 2006 - and Nvidia. For a while, it was a real fight. AMD paid $5.4 billion for ATI, and in the second quarter of 2010, Radeon cards briefly overtook Nvidia in discrete graphics shipments. However, AMD had a problem: it couldn’t really afford ATI. It wrote off $1.6 billion of goodwill from the deal about a year after it closed, and its PC chip business kept struggling.

By early 2015, AMD’s CPU and GPU revenue was down 38% on the year, and the company was close to negative book value. Its quarterly R&D budget had fallen to its lowest level since 2004, with Nvidia spending nearly half as much again. Radeon cards stayed on the same Graphics Core Next architecture for about seven years before RDNA arrived in 2019. By then, Nvidia had already launched its RTX cards with dedicated ray tracing hardware and Tensor cores for AI, and it never gave that lead back.

Intel was the only company with pockets deep enough to try breaking back in. Its first go, Larrabee, was cancelled as a consumer graphics chip in December 2009. It finally got there in 2022, when the Arc A770 went on sale from $329, alongside the cheaper A750. Both arrived after repeated delays and struggled with older DirectX 9 games, and many observers - RPS included - put their chances of breaking up the Nvidia-AMD duopoly at low. By the time then-hardware editor James returned to the A750 in 2023, Intel had drastically improved its drivers, bringing big gains to both general performance and DX9 compatibility. Even then, the Arc series had yet to prove it could work well at launch, without the need to be ironed out across months of updates.

The second generation did indeed fare better, with the Arc B580 successfully selling out at $249 in December 2024. But that still barely impacted the wider industry, with Intel sitting at just 1% of graphics card shipments in the third quarter of 2025 and around 2% this spring, when Nvidia took roughly 90% of the 12.5 million cards shipped.

It now looks like Intel is on its way back out of gaming graphics cards. In April, leaker Jaykihn claimed that its next-generation Celestial gaming cards had been cancelled "long ago," and the latest rumours say B580 supply could be cut so Intel can sell more Arc Pro cards for, surprise surprise, AI work. It’s important to note that Intel hasn’t confirmed any of that, and one of its execs has said that Arc isn’t leaving its PC roadmap. Still, Intel had everything 3dfx didn’t: the cash, the PC makers on side, and the same APIs as everyone else. But money can’t buy two decades of Nvidia and AMD fixing their drivers game by game, and it seems to have decided its capital is better spent on AI anyway.

Evidently, the question of where all the other GPU makers went does not have one single answer. Some couldn’t afford the rising costs, some couldn’t keep pace with a new Nvidia chip every six months, and some lost their cheap business to Intel’s integrated graphics or went under when the dot-com bubble burst. Left over was a Nvidia/ATI (later AMD) duopoly, and PC gamers haven’t exactly done well out of it. We saw the RTX 4080 launch at $1,199 in 2022, nearly twice the 3080’s price, and the ongoing, AI-driven RAM shortage has pushed prices higher still.

In 1998, 47 companies wanted your money. Now there are two, and the bigger one, Nvidia, sells nine of every 10 graphics cards - yet still makes most of its money from data centres. Eighteen years on, it's a bad time to be a PC gamer, and nobody’s in a hurry to make things any better.

Jennifer Svedberg-Yen loves Mass Effect's "attention to detail in the narrative and the storylines"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The writer behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 says the recent closure of Mass Effect and Dragon Age studio BioWare "broke my heart," and she's currently playing the first two sci-fi games in the series "in honor."

Speaking in a recent interview with GamesBeat, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen talks about the importance of narrative, noting that "anybody who's interested in franchises or IP as a broader potential can’t discount the power of story." She adds that "I love a lot of games that have no narrative at all," so it's not to say that one is better than the other, but she points to the Mass Effect games as excellent examples of games that nail their storylines. Needless to say, last month's studio closure was a huge blow for her.

"I'm playing Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 right now, in honor of BioWare. That broke my heart," she says.

Svedberg-Yen points to "the attention to detail in the narrative and the storylines" as something she particularly enjoys. "The way that they play out through the three games when you import your storylines over is incredible," she adds. "I love that. I feel like that's a remarkable achievement. I'd love to see more games like that."

Good thing EA didn't just cancel a new Mass Effect game then, huh? Oh, wait.

Mass Effect 5's cancellation was, sadly, announced last month along with BioWare's closure. It was apparently set to be called Mass Effect: Universe – a name one former dev says was partially inspired by the fact that "you had so many choices that you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes."

Whether Mass Effect could be saved by being sold to another studio is another matter that former BioWare devs can't seem to agree on. One previously shared his belief that "EA never actually sells anything," while one of the studio's former executive producers, Mark Darrah, said that while no one working on the series at EA "might make them more likely to sell off those IPs," it equally "might also make them more likely to try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault."

#3873. Guide: Who Is the GTA 6 Cover Art Girl and Is She Based on a Real Person?

What we know about the GTA 6 cover art girl so far

GTA 6 is going live now worldwide, and that means you might have more questions about the cover girl on the box art. In this GTA 6 guide, we're covering who is the GTA 6 cover art girl and is she based on a real person?

On this page: Who Is the GTA 6 Cover Art Girl and Is She Based on a Real Person?

With GTA 6 now available, we'll be able to find out if the cover art girl actually appears in the game. Up until now, Rockstar hasn't commented on who she is.

At the time of writing, with the game going live worldwide, there hasn't been any evidence of the GTA 6 cover girl being found in the game.

GTA games have often had women on their box arts, but it's important to note this doesn't necessarily mean they'll play an important role in the story — or even appear at all. History has taught us the girls on the front cover can sometimes appear in minor roles within the plot, but they're usually not critical to the story.

For example, the cover girl from GTA 5, the girl taking a picture in a red bikini, doesn't appear in the game whatsoever. It is the same for GTA 4: the girl wearing a red top and licking a lollipop isn't in the game. In fact, in terms of the mainline entries, you'd need to go back to Vice City for an example of the cover girl actually being in the game.

As such, there's a chance the GTA 6 cover girl is purely for promotional purposes — she might not be in the game at all.

So, there's a fairly good chance the GTA 6 cover girl won't be in the game itself, but is she based on a real person? While developer Rockstar hasn't said yet, the Internet believes it's found someone with a very, very strong resemblance.

Gabriela Chiquin, who is an influencer, DJ, and musician from Venezuela, looks a lot like the GTA 6 cover girl. In a number of Instagram posts, she has her hair curled similarly to the cover girl, and wears green clothing. The pictures of her in green are from a few years ago, so they weren't taken in response to the attention she's gotten from the link to GTA 6.

Having caught wind of the similarities, she said in an Instagram post: "I want to thank the entire GTA community for so much love. I never imagined receiving so many messages, comments, and memes." She doesn't actually say whether she is the GTA 6 cover girl or not, however.

The cover girls for its game isn't something Rockstar usually makes a big deal out of, so it's unlikely we'll ever get official confirmation that Chiquin is the actual inspiration for the GTA 6 cover girl. Still, there's a very clear resemblance here, and the Internet managed to make the connection within days.

#3872. Don't expect more information on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel "for some time," Bethesda says

After Bethesda formally named The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel earlier this month, some series fans were hopeful that more news wasn't far behind. Skyrim is 15 years old today (11th November) after all, but Bethesda Game Studios has since dashed those hopes into oblivion.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any big announcements tomorrow," the social media account wrote. "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything new on Sentinel for some time."

The Elder Scrolls fans have already been waiting for the series' next mainline follow-up for, erm, also quite some time. Specifically, Skyrim came out in 2011, The Elder Scrolls 6's first reveal trailer reared its head in 2018, and BGS' Starfield took to the stars in 2023 - a wait so long that it had even the most faithful among us questioning if a new Elder Scrolls could ever recapture the series' magic.

So, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

In the meantime, Bethesda isn't letting Skyrim's 15th anniversary go by without a few celebrations. For one, the seminal role-playing game is deeply discounted on all platforms, in the very unlikely scenario you haven't tried it out yet.

The Elder Scrolls Online Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim is also joining the festivities by adding the Greymoor Chapter into the base game for free, giving everyone access to a few famous Skyrim locales and more. A brand-new, separate Golden Pursuit campaign will let you earn some Skyrim-centric goodies up until 2nd December, as well.

#3871. Minerva Rising is a Frostpunk-meets-Silo underground city builder in which rebel citizens can hack your camera

Minerva Rising is a post-apocalyptic city builder in which your city extends deep underground, divided into levels with their own resources, industries, and communities. You are an artificial intelligence with overall control, but watch out: if you alienate the population of any particular level by, say, forgetting to supply them with oxygen, subversives may rise up and cut your feed, blinding you to their activities.

I'm keen to know whether it's possible for every level to lose faith in you and hack your cameras, reducing the game to a pile of "SIGNAL NOT FOUND" messages. I'm also imagining turning the feeds back on and discovering that everybody is having a massive orgy. Stupid sexy vault dwellers! You'll go forth and multiply when Deep Thought tells you to, and not a second before.

When solo developer Jonny Strellman emailed me about Minerva Rising, he framed it as "Frostpunk meets Silo", Silo being that apparently quite good Apple TV+ show starring Rebecca Ferguson. (I assume if you're reading this, I don't need to introduce you to Frostpunk.) It's got at least one thing neither of those productions has: in-game footage of Steamboat Willy, displayed on propaganda screens you might set up, if you want to buoy cave-dweller morale with thoughts of the copyright-expired world before. Alternatively, you can encourage them to fall in love with the caves themselves, which may harbour luxurious waterfalls and incandescent fungus.

Who needs the sun? Can't get sunburn from a glowing mushroom, can you? Look, citizens of level 13: you'd better overcome your distaste for giant toadstools or I'm turning the power off again. Damn it, you stay the hell away from my factory reset button. "WELCOME TO MICROSOFT WINDOWS 95." Balls! "[✓] SHOW THIS WELCOME SCREEN NEXT TIME YOU START WINDOWS." Right, that's it. I don't appear to have any military options in this game, but I'm pretty sure I can redesignate your whole cave as a compost heap.

"Cut through new strata of earth and ethics each playthrough," the Steam page enthuses. "No two games will be the same. One run might face blight and starvation, while another might be low on coal for producing power. Your decisions and the resources you find provide different challenges each time you play. Even if your people live to see the sun again, there are varied and sundry ways to get there." There's no release date for it yet. If you'd rather build cities in the other direction, check out Stario: Haven Tower.
