If you own a pair of headphones in GTA 6, you can even listen to your favorite shows while on foot for the very first time

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar has made some vital changes to the way that you listen to music, access podcasts, and change radio stations in GTA 6. You can even listen to music outside of your vehicles for the first time, so long as you have the necessary headgear purchased and equipped.

Below you'll find a quick rundown of how to listen to music in GTA 6, how to access on-demand podcasts, and where to buy your own headphones to listen to your favorite songs from the GTA 6 soundtrack while you're roaming around the world of Leonida.

There are radios in GTA 6 everywhere. In your safehouse, in whatever vehicles you're driving around, and sometimes you'll find them out in the world too. Thankfully, how to use a radio and change stations in GTA 6 rarely changes.

When you're driving a car you'll want to hold Left on the D-pad to access the radio controls. This is also true for radios in the world, bikes, boats, and planes. Whilst you are holding Left on the D-Pad, you can scroll between all of the radio stations either with L1/LB and R1/RB, or with the right thumbstick. Select the station that you want, stop holding the D-pad button, and it'll start playing. You can also go into this menu and press X/A to turn off the radio entirely.

You can also activate 'On Demand' programming in GTA 6 like podcasts in a similar way. Activate that radio menu again by holding Left on the D-pad, only now you want to press Down with the right thumbstick. This will let you access all of the podcasts which are available to you. You can even press Square/ X on each to scroll between episodes, and then press X/A to play.

Tip: If you actively go into the on-demand section of the radio menu, you can pause the podcast that you're listening to. Head back in here later (regardless of whether you're on foot or back in a vehicle) and it'll sync playback up to where you left off.

Buying a set of headphones allows you to listen to radio and podcasts while outside of a vehicle. To get headphones, open the GTA 6 Index and scroll to the Style tab. In here you're looking for the 'Electronics' option which will display all shops that sell these items, ordered by the one that's closest to your current location. Head over to one of these stores to purchase a pair of headphones or earbuds – these range upwards of $100 for a basic set through to more luxurious models depending on the store, and remember that both Jason and Lucia will need to purchase their own.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Once you have purchased headphones in GTA 6, you'll need to equip them. Hold L1/LB to open your loadout and press R1/RB to navigate to the items tab. The second slot in the wheel is for headgear; navigate to this slot with the right thumbstick and press X to equip your headphones. From there, it's as easy as holding Left on the D-pad to access the radio stations and on-demand podcasts.

If you bought headphones and now can't find them in the menu, it's possible that you have lost them in combat. If you get attacked by the cops or a civilian in the world with headphones equipped, these can get knocked to the ground. Don't forget to pick them back up once you're done brawling, otherwise they will be lost forever!

JamesI've got a date with Derelikt, a retro survival-horror FPS with just a dash of immsim keycode hunting. I'm not expecting gee-oh-tee-why material but I do respect any game whose minimum system requirements read, in their entirety, "Sound Card: Toaster Spec".

#3786. The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting a New Game Plus mode in next week's update

UPDATE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

New Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

There'll be new versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker update 1.2 are:

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, currently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions."

Elsewhere in Update 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful."

The Wanted Level goes up to six now, but it isn't for the faint of heart

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In the entirety of my time playing the game for review, I was only able to reach a six-star Wanted level in GTA 6 the one time. That's partially because I was hell bent on maintaining a 'Professional' Criminal Profile in GTA 6, and also because it's really difficult to activate. You have to really be on a bit of a mad one to get this level of heat coming down on you.

If you aren't aware, GTA 6 brought back six stars to the Wanted system. You typically gain heat for doing everything from trespassing to petty crime to big bank robberies, with different numbers of stars indicating the volume of cops (and eventually military) who respond to try and bring you in.

My only six-star encounter in GTA 6 was the result of a firefight with a regular citizen that went awry, the accidental throwing of a grenade at a bunch of cop cars, and then a high-speed pursuit which lasted for well-over 15 minutes and eventually resulted in me hijacking an aeroplane in a desperate attempt to gain some ground. As it turns out, it's only mass destruction and loss of life which will get you six-stars of trouble in GTA 6.

The problem with getting a 6-star wanted level in GTA 6 is that there's actually no way to resolve it. Once you've got that sort of heat on you, the cops and the military will not stop in their pursuit of you. My poor aeroplane lasted just minutes after jets were dispatched to bring me crashing down to Earth.

Interestingly enough, there is a GTA 6 cheat code to raise the wanted level, but no matter how many times I put in the activation code, it would never go above five stars. Which is all to say, the game really is only giving you a 6 star wanted level in GTA 6 when you really deserve it. And then once you've got it… settle in for some pretty outrageous carnage.

#3783. Magic: The Gathering animated series Planeswalker is coming to Netflix in 2027

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

The title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the company wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

#3782. Missed something on your first go around The Blood of Dawnwalker? I've got good news, as next week's update adds in new game plus

A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration."

Overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests."

#3781. RPG Maker U2U launches January 28, 2027

Role-playing game creation software RPG Maker U2U will launch for PC via Steam on January 28, 2027, Gotcha Gotcha Games announced.

Availability of the “P2D Map Editor Demo,” which was originally planned to end today, has also been extended up until the software’s launch.

Here is an overview of the software, via Gotcha Gotcha Games:

RPG Maker U2U is the latest entry in the RPG Maker series of easy to use game development tools. With the addition of the new P2D system for adding depth and new light & shadow effects, create world of rich detail and immersion like never before!

RPG Maker U2U expands traditional 2D maps with depth, light, shadow, and a variety of beautiful effects with the new “P2D” (Perspective 2D) function. Create the world of your imagination and expression like never before in latest entry in the RPG Maker franchise!

P2D combine the intuitive simplicity of top-down mapping with true spatial elevation: add slopes, ledges, multi-story buildings, overpasses, and more with ease! Create towns, dungeons, interiors, and overworlds with a level of depth that exceeds traditional 2D map creation!

Out of the box you’ll have access to lots of visual effects. Camera effects like depth of field, weather effects like rain and fog, and dramatic lighting and shadows for interior lighting, street lamps, and other uses! When these effects are combined with the 3D verticality offered by P2D, creators will be able to make maps with strong aesthetics and mood for more immersive storytelling.

No coding required, so getting started is a snap! Create maps, game events, and configure your combat with U2U’s easy and intuitive editor.

And if you’re not an artist, don’t worry! U2U ships with a variety of different characters, monsters, visual effects, music, sound effects and more! Everything you need to get started with no additional downloads needed.

More than 100 pre-built P2D maps are included and ready for use!

Use the dedicated P2D map editor to quickly make place pre-made objects or make new objects from with provided blocks to create worlds tailored to your vision.

Re-use your existing RPG Maker MV and RPG Maker MZ assets as P2D map assets! See your familiar assets take on new life with the addition of P2D’s lighting and depth effects!

As the user interface and user experience are built around the RPG Maker MZ workflow, RPG Maker U2U should feel immediately familiar to series veterans.

A note of caution: conversion of project data and plug-ins created with previous RPG Maker titles is not supported.

After Jensen Huang's departure from the company last week, Nvidia is now on the hunt for its next permanent CEO. Speaking in the Q&A section of Nvidia's Q3 2027 earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones says the directors are taking the search "very seriously."

"We're going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates" says Jones. "The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully."

Jones also says the company "won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person," but Amazon boss Jeff Bezos seems to think that hiring outside of Nvidia would be a mistake.

"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," says Bezos, speaking at the Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday (via Yahoo Finance). "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding, and so I would always think that's a last resort."

Nvidia is currently being helmed by CFO Collette Kress as an interim chief, while recent reports have suggested that Huang may make a potential return to the company.

The ex-Nvidia chief said that he would come back "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America" after a petition calling for his reinstatement, but Nvidia's board has poured cold water on this idea already.

"The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," says Jones during the earnings call opening statements.

#3779. Call of Duty Endowment marks Remembrance Day with veterans' Valor Pack push

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, says it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

#3778. From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws

Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff."

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

You can overwrite and load into any of these save slots in GTA 6. It's also worth mentioning that there is a single, secret 16th slot that is reserved for an auto-save which triggers after missions, if you're wasted, busted, or have some sort of major encounter in the open world.

The save system will also disable if you activate any GTA 6 cheats, forcing you to quit out of the game and reload a save that wasn't revelling in pure chaos.

#3776. Congratulations to people who feel mean shooting random NPCs, because GTA 6 tries "to provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy

When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a new interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

In any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

Well, whaddaya know? Turns out all you need to make a great videogame is around a decade of time, the GDP of a BRICS nation, and a marketing machine pervasive to the point of totalitarianism. The reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6—Rockstar's sequel to that game that would splash "GOURANGA!" on the screen when you ran over enough people—are in. People like it a lot.

No, really, they're out of their gourd for this one, folks. GTA 6 might just be the most absurdly hyped game in history, and yet the mad lads at Rockstar really seem to have pulled it off. Of course, the game's true test—its review on PC Gamer dot com and its accompanying magazine—hasn't happened yet. We'll have to wait for the all-but-certain PC port for that. For now, you can read our impressions of the console version here.

But our console brethren have been putting pen to paper to get their thoughts down, and the reviews for GTA 6 are flowing thick and fast. Here's a sample platter of them, to give you an idea of just how nuts people are going for this thing.

GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain paints a picture of Leonida that overflows with detail, calling it "a game of staggering scope and scale obsessed with small details that could be lost in its vastness, a giant haystack full of needles that you’ll constantly find, creating delight in their improbable discovery". I get the impression that a year from now, five years, ten years, there will still be people rushing to subreddits and forums (if we still have those) to ask if others have seen this or that little detail Rockstar tucked into some obscure corner of its humungous world.

A second perfect score from the gang at IGN, whose Luke Reilly had a great time doing things like:

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Most of which you could feasibly cram into a game whose goal was to simulate my dad, but in GTA 6 it all forms part of a world that constantly surprises you with things to do. "I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it", writes Reilly, adding that—despite having beaten the game with 120 hours of playtime under his belt—"While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit".

Our brothers in arms at GR note that GTA 6 is an improvement on every entry in the series before it: "there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments", writes Josh West, who calls the game (affectionately) "the ultimate time vampire" where "every one of your actions ultimately impacts the lives of Jason and Lucia". Honestly, sounds like a nerve-wracking amount of responsibility for me.

The New York Times – Too stately to give a review score but it's an "NYT Critic’s Pick"

You know a videogame has broken containment when the grey lady is getting in on the review beat. The NYT's Yussef Cole zeroed in on GTA 6's heart in his review: the relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos—"This is a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful", he writes, noting that players can choose to hold hands with their paramour at the touch of a button. We've come a little ways from beating people to death with dildos, folks (though you may well still be able to do that; I'd be surprised if you couldn't).

Giant Bomb (shoutout to Charlie Tunoku) joins in with the hosannahs for GTA 6, describing it as one of those games that feels like a step up for the medium as a whole. "Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar’s best game", writes Dan Ryckert. "In the thirteen years between entries of one of the biggest franchises in entertainment, fans’ expectations grew to a level that felt unrealistic. Somehow, Rockstar has managed to overdeliver on the most hyped video game of all time".

The Guardian's Keza MacDonald writes that Rockstar's Leonida is so realistic as to defy belief, but that in its humid, gator-ridden byways you will find scope for both "foulmouthed, OTT chaos—as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre". It is a game, it seems, that is almost too big and varied to squeeze into something like a regular review. "it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start". But you bet those experiences are many, varied, and shockingly fleshed-out.

Bloomberg – Unscored, but you get the picture

Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, who you may recognise from videogame scoops, is in love with GTA 6 too. He opens with a description of one of the random events that can happen to players in the game, in which he witnessed a crash and found himself enlisted into an NPC's scam to sue a parody of Amazon for millions. "Incidents like this, elaborate depictions of a heightened reality, happen constantly in Grand Theft Auto 6", he writes. "The joy of Grand Theft Auto VI, much like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Elden Ring before it, comes from discovering its world’s delights and seeing how it reacts to your actions".

It perhaps tells us something that the only non-perfect score on this list is… a 4.5/5 overflowing with praise. Slant's Justin Clark calls GTA 6 "something above and beyond anything the AAA gaming space has ever produced", and has oodles of praise for its rich and hyper-detailed open world. He also thinks that, you know, what's an open world compared to the "first truly meaningful interactive relationship between two semi-realistic grown-ass adults in the entire medium", which Rockstar has also managed to pull off here. "Home, for Jason and Lucia, is each other. Whether there’s $2 million or $2 in their bank accounts, and whether they got it from an honest job or by decimating a metropolitan police force with a grenade launcher, letting these two make a home in each other is the only investment that truly matters—and the best one Rockstar could have ever made, creatively."

One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War.

#3773. Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks

The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into early access.

To say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be big or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

You can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

#3772. Ubisoft is reportedly making a new Rainbow Six Vegas game, nearly two decades after Vegas 2

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

GTA 6 is a wild ride – but can you replay missions once you've completed them?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Here's something that's a little surprising about Rockstar's long-awaited return to Vice City: There is no way to replay missions in GTA 6.

With over 90 main story missions in GTA 6, some of which are an absolute riot of a time while others feature pretty substantial branching paths that help shape your GTA 6 Criminal Profile system, it's no surprise that many of you are wondering how to replay your favorite moments from the campaign.

Sadly, after playing the game for over 100 hours for my GTA 6 review, I can confirm that there's simply no option to do so. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. GTA 5 did let you replay missions easy enough, but that was a way to let you back into key moments to try and complete skill challenges – Rockstar has since moved all of the GTA 6 challenges into its own spot in the progress menu. They are now far broader in scope, and primarily used to unlock GTA 6 cheats once you've wrapped up the story.

If you're worried about missing anything or wanting to play key moments from a chapter again, I would recommend that you learn the ins and outs of the GTA 6 save system – this lets you keep and load back into 15 different sessions. Otherwise, you'd have to start a whole new game just to replay a mission in GTA 6!

#3769. Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

AMD landed itself in hot water with gamers a couple of weeks back by saying the quiet part out loud: CEO Dr. Lisa Su announced that it was a "datacentre-first company" in a call with investors, who were likely to want to hear that sorta thing. Yet upon reaching gamers' ears, the news wasn't so well received.

Now, AMD Japan has tried to settle things down by proclaiming "AMD loves gamers."

To be fair, those two statements aren't mutually exclusive. AMD can be datacentre first, and absolutely is, and still claim to care about gaming. Though when supply for key components is tight and prices are rising, we're definitely looking for a little more than kind words at this time.

What makes matters worse is that AMD Japan also added: "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else."

In Q3, AMD made more than double the cash from its datacentre segment ($8.5 billion) than its client and gaming segment ($3.7 billion)—the latter includes various Ryzen, as well as Radeon, products. Pure gaming revenue was a mere $773 million, and dropping fast, whereas datacentre revenue was up 97%.

So, from a purely business perspective, AMD is undoubtedly all in on datacentres. I don't like to admit it, but it makes sense for a company owned by shareholders to go after the biggest growth market. But all the more reason not to claim an undying love for gamers—it just doesn't pass muster.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

AMD Japan is responding to a tweet from our sister site, Tom's Hardware, who had reported that the company's CEO had attended a store opening for a new Micro Center in Austin, Texas and was handing out autographed graphics cards and swag bags to lucky attendees. So, in that sense, AMD can claim to have helped a handful of gamers directly. An RX 9070 XT signed by Lisa Su may hold its value more than one signed by Jensen Huang.

Nevertheless, the post on X hasn't been too well received. A reader note has been added to note AMD's claim to be a datacentre first company, and the replies are a bit of a dumpster fire.

Truth be told, it's not a good time to claim to care about the gamers, whether there's any truth to the claim or not. From graphics cards to SSDs, we're stuck with extremely high prices, beyond most reasonable budgets, and few exciting product launches to note—except monitors. Thank God for monitors.

#3765. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Big Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

Peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

Just because you saw GTA 6 first-person mode in the leaks doesn't necessarily mean it's in the final game

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

First-person mode for GTA 6 featured in one of the various pre-release leaks, so naturally a lot of you are wondering how to activate it now that you're taking your first steps into Leonida. It's a gorgeous world that's packed with detail, and I'm with you in wanting to get a closer look at some of the gorgeous environments.

I'm sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but there is no first-person mode in GTA 6. It's a little disappointing, given that GTA 5 received the functionality as part of the PS4/Xbox One release in 2014. Sadly, Rockstar has opted out of giving you the option to switch between first-person and third-person in GTA 6, and it's unlikely that it will come in the future.

That all being said, there are certain instances where you can look through the eyes of Jason and Lucia. If you press L2/LT to focus on a character and then click L3 and R3 you can enter first-person in GTA 6 to get a better look at specific items. You can also enter first-person mode when you pull out your phone and when you're in certain vehicles, but that's about it.

If you have modified a weapon in GTA 6 with a scope, you're also able to click R3 whilst you are aiming down sights to enter first-person mode for precision aiming. That's pretty great, all things considered, but if you were hoping to run through the GTA 6 missions in first-person, that's not going to happen.

And no, there aren't any GTA 6 cheats that will let you go into first-person either. Trust me, I checked.

#3763. "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

"Let's see how the project handles real player traffic"

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics."

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

"They may come out five years from now, and the world may not care."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It may be hard to notice what with all the Grand Theft Auto 6-ness happening right now, but the games industry has had a very rough last few years. This isn't to say no great games have come out this year. I've actually had a great time, what with Resident Evil Requiem, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Big Walk—oh and I've heard that Queen's Domain is rather good also.

But the issue of how big studios are able to balance their budget still stands. “Around content, AAA is under the most amount of threat," former Take-Two CEO, Ben Feder says in an interview with The Game Business. "They’re not big enough to really be platforms on the one hand, and they’re not small enough to really innovate on the other. If you talk to the major publishers, they cannot figure out a way to make a game for less than $300 million, and that to me is just not sustainable."

We now know for sure that GTA 6 is a winner: just look at this review score round up. But there are some worried that replicating this success is nigh impossible for any other studio. As Feder puts it, not everyone can take their "entire development team, putting them in a time capsule, burying them in the ground, and five years later they pop out and say, 'Voila, here it is.'" Most studios simply do not have the capacity or funds to have a team solely working on a project for around a decade.

"Three to five years ago, that was reasonable because we know what they’re building, it’s good IP, they have a niche, and we know what the world’s going to look like when they pop out of the ground," Feder adds. "Today, while they’re underground, on the surface of planet Earth all of this change is happening, not just technologically but also with respect to consumer tastes and expectations. They may come out five years from now, and the world may not care."

Feder goes on to explain that GTA 6 is the exception to this rule as it's able to deliver "escape velocity". I take this to mean the ridiculous amounts of hype and money that surround this game is why it's able to retain this old way of working. "Scale matters there, and you need an enormous amount of capital to do that,” Feder says. "The amount of capital required starts with a 'B' not with an 'M', for sure."

#3761. Blade Runner 2099 bosses hint at a possible "triple-A" Blade Runner game in the future - just don't expect it any time soon

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

It's possible to advance from day to night so long as you follow this one trick

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you're taking your first steps into Key Lento right now, you've no doubt realized that the day and night cycle is considerably longer than it ever was in Los Santos. So you are no doubt wondering how to change the time of day in GTA 6. It's possible, but it takes a little effort to do so.

The time of day in GTA 6 works dynamically, meaning that it gradually shifts as you're out in the world committing crimes, driving to destinations, and completing activities. There's big changes between day and night beyond the color palette change too. The police response times are a little longer at night, especially if you're far outside of a major city, while you may also find that buildings that you can enter are more likely to be occupied at night rather than day – you know, when the NPCs have jobs to be at.

So if you want to change the time of day in GTA 6 for whatever reason, the easiest way to do this is to go and rest up in the bed of your safehouse. Once Jason or Lucia is resting on the mattress, you have the option of pressing Square/X to sleep. From there you can choose to sleep until whatever time of day that you want to. A similar effect will happen if you try to fast travel in GTA 6 across longer destinations.

So that's how you can change the time of day in GTA 6, at least until you've got the story wrapped up. Once you're in the endgame, there is one of the GTA 6 cheats which is wholly dedicated to moving the time of day around – but you'll need to unlock that specific functionality before you can do so.

#3759. Phasmophobia ‘Resonance’ update launches November 24

Kinetic Games will release the “Resonance” update for Phasmophobia on November 14, which introduces new investigation equipment, technical upgrades, and several gameplay improvements.

“We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters’ kits can add as much value as possible in investigations, and the ‘Resonance’ update has been an exciting opportunity not only to freshen up Sound Sensors and Voice Recognition, but to add a completely new piece of equipment with the Dowsing Rods,” said Kinetic Games CEO and game director Daniel Knight in a press release. “We’re looking forward to hearing how the community get on with them. ‘Resonance’ also brings Phasmophobia‘s move to Unity 6—while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive. It’s been a huge undertaking for our whole team, and we hope our players enjoy everything ‘Resonance’ has to offer.”

Here is a brief overview of the update, via Kinetic Games:

The “Resonance” update also marks Phasmophobia‘s transition to the Unity 6 engine, bringing technical improvements in the form of more realistic lighting to enhance immersion, and improved stability. Additional settings are being introduced to the game too, with expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness accessibility settings.

Addressing recent community feedback, “Resonance” will also be bringing numerous fixes for several prominent bugs. The update will also introduce a new player conduct warning system that will warn players before receiving an account ban, except in cases of severe violations. Full details are available in the blog notes here.

Phasmophobia is currently in Early Access for PlayStation 5 with PlayStation VR2 support, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam, and is coming to Switch 2. The game has surpassed five million copies sold on consoles and 28 million copies sold overall.

#3758. "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power."

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

#3757. Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service

"Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

On Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox announced earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

If you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he announced the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

"Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material."

"You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," says ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...]."

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

#3755. Cyberpunk 2077 mod Torrent adds 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

Learn how to switch characters and issue commands to Jason and Lucia in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There are two playable characters in GTA 6 to switch between – Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. They are partners in crime, working together to make enough money in Leonida to build a better future. That means that you'll need to engage with both characters to get the most out of your time with the world. Thankfully, Rockstar Games has built in a number of different ways for Jason and Lucia to interact.

Whether you're playing through one of the main GTA 6 missions or just exploring the wide open world of Leonida, the game is undoubtedly at its best when Jason and Lucia are working together. Below I'm going to break down how to switch characters in GTA 6, how to meet up with your partner, and give you some top tips on how to work as a more effective pair when you're engaging in a little crime.

You aren't able to immediately switch characters in GTA 6. The option will become available once you hit a certain milestone in Chapter 2. Once both of the characters are available, hold right on the d-pad and press R1/RB to switch between the characters.

There are infrequent restrictions to swapping characters in GTA 6. Sometimes your partner will be busy, with a darkened character profile once you hold left on the d-pad indicating that you can't switch right away. Keep checking in though, as they will eventually be available.

Tip: Jason and Lucia will sometimes have their own tasks which require you to switch characters. If you see either a J or an L on the map it means that the mission must be played solo.

Checking in with your partner regularly is a great way to improve your relationship status in GTA 6. There's a couple of ways to do this, but the easiest is to message them through WhatUp – hold right on the d-pad and press Triangle / Y if there is a blue icon about a character's profile picture, or press up on the d-pad and navigate to the relevant app in the GTA 6 phone menu.

Tip: When Jason and Lucia are together, you can use L2/LT to focus on your partner. This will prompt conversations, and give you the opportunity to share items you are holding like food and drink.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Meeting up with your partner is essential throughout GTA 6. The easiest way to reach out is to hold right on the d-pad and press Triangle/Y. Alternatively, you can also navigate to the Contacts app on your phone and call your partner. This will prompt them to drive to where you're currently situated on the GTA 6 map; if you have a destination set, your partner will meet you there.

Tip: If you spend a full day together, look for visual and audio cues that it's time to head home together and get in some much needed rest. A little heart icon will appear around your residence on the map, while sometimes your partner will raise it as an idea in casual conversation.

You don't always need to do the heavy lifting on driving. If you are close to your personal vehicle, you can hold Right on the d-pad to ask your partner to drive. Once you're in the passenger seat, open up the map and set a destination, and they will start making their way there.

The AI pathfinding is solid when your partner is at the wheel, but you can hold Right on the d-pad to issue them instructions to speed up and slow down. You can also use this functionality to ask your partner to split up and take the vehicle with them –a great way of lowering your wanted level in GTA 6.

Tip: If you're at the wheel while being chased by the cops, you can switch characters to take control of the passenger. Just remember that incapacitating police vehicles (even non-lethally) will contribute to a Hardened Criminal Profile in GTA 6.

Whether you're sticking up a local convenience store for petty cash or launching an assault on a bank for a big pay day, you can undertake robberies both solo and as a pair. If you go into the map and hover over the icon of the location you're planning to hit, it'll denote the security – if it's medium to high, you'll want to consider bringing your partner along for the ride.

Before starting a robbery, hold Right on the d-pad to open up some new options for your eventual escape from the location. You can ask your partner to wait in the car while you go inside, helping to save some precious seconds before the cops show up.

Once a robbery is in-progress, you can hold Right on the d-pad to ask them to come in from the car to provide backup. Using this method is also a great way to hand over one of your weapons if they need it; each character can only hold two stash bags filled with ill-gotten gains at any one time, but you can also throw these over to your partner to carry.

Tip: Committing a robbery is a fairly intuitive process. If you directly threaten guards or cashiers, this will prompt your partner to support you and hold a weapon on them while you move through a building.

Once you're together, it is possible to have your partner leave for whatever reason. Hold Right on the d-pad to get the option to split up from your partner, leaving you solo with the character you're in primary control of. This can be done at any point while you're exploring the world, but there may be restrictions in certain missions.

If you've got the cops chasing you through the streets, you do have the option to split up. There's two benefits of this: the first is that they can split away from you and distract the cops, reducing some of the heat on you and removing one of the conditions to the GTA 6 Wanted Level you're trying to outrun. The second is that they can also head off and use one of the fences to sell any stolen goods that they have on them without you needing to be there – although, word of warning, the price you'll get for the score may be reduced.

Tip: If you ask a partner to split off from you after a robbery, keep an eye out for a message from them on WhatUp. They will usually ask if they should sell the score or come meet back up with you, and ignoring these messages will have a negative impact on your relationship.

#3751. GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach which the company claim cost them $5 million

Hacker was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

Police are still investigating the motive.

Police have arrested a suspect after a drive-by shooting at an office campus in Tustin, California, which is home to Xbox-owned studio inXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

"Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Police have not given a motive, and the suspect has not been named.

InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is currently working on Clockwork Revolution.

A stable 30 fps on RDNA 2 hardware with a game this stunning is promising.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

From what we're already seeing of Grand Theft Auto 6 on console, it's boding very well for a future PC release. It might only be targeting 30 fps on console, but with how stable that is and with the graphics looking so stunning on older PS5/PS5 Pro hardware, I've got high hopes for how it might run on our gaming PCs.

Digital Foundry (DF) has taken one for the team here by doing some performance testing on an inferior platform (cheap shot, I'm sorry). And judging from the screenshots, videos, and frame rate analysis so far, GTA 6 looks very much next-gen in terms of scale, scope, and fidelity.

We're talking fine detail on the local scale combined with open, bustling sight lines to the horizon, depending on your vantage point. All very noticeably saturated by incredible ray traced lighting, and running at a stable 30 fps on the PS5 Pro.

It's hard to describe how fantastic GTA looks. It does seem like a new era for open world games.

What particularly impresses me, judging from DF's gameplay and graphics shots, is how seamlessly fine detail combines with great lighting and breaks into long distance views.

One minute you're inside a bustling store, with incredibly realistic ambient lighting and reflections thanks to the ray tracing implementation (plus ray traced shadows on the PS5 Pro), admiring the stranded hair on all the NPCs and the little touches such as drinks actually draining in the bottle you drink from.

The next, you can be looking across the entire city without losing any noticeable detail. This seamlessness does make it seem like a real, lively world.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

A large part of this immersion seems to come from the lighting. You're getting full ray traced global illumination, apparently at 1440p resolution which, on the PS5 Pro, reportedly looks more like 4K (and on the base PS5 apparently looks like it might be 1440p upscaled). The PS5 (non-Pro) version looks a little more blurry and lacks the level of shadow definition, but for the most part both versions look great. At least as far as I can tell from DF's footage, anyway.

All of the above is only good news if it runs well, and thankfully on this front it looks like it does. Yes, we're only talking 30 fps, but on the PS5 Pro version, at least, that's a very stable 30 fps. DF says there wasn't a single noticeable stutter or drop in over 50 hours of gameplay, and it's only when you start blowing up cars on the street that you get brief drops down to as low as 24 fps.

The PS5 (non-Pro) is different, struggling to consistently maintain 30 fps even when just driving around the city. But that console has significantly worse hardware compared to the Pro, so it's to be expected—the GPU in the PS5 has just 36 compute units (CUs) compared to the PS5 Pro's 60.

As far as playing GTA 6 on PC is concerned, I think this means we can be hopeful. The PS5 Pro's AMD GPU does have some RDNA 3/4 features, but for the most part it's an RDNA 2 chip. RDNA 2 graphics cards for PC are Radeon RX 6000-series ones. So, even with an older PC using a graphics card that is two generations old, it's possible you'll be able to get the gorgeous graphics you see on the PS5 Pro at a stable 30 fps.

At what settings? Well, that remains to be seen. But considering we'll almost certainly get some more customisation options over on PC, we should be able to eke out as much performance as we can from it, tailored to our hardware.

If you have a newer PC with a newer graphics card, I'd be hoping for 60 fps+ performance, and for that to be stable. The RX 9070 XT, for instance, should outperform a PS5 Pro considerably, despite only having a handful of extra CUs, thanks to the much newer architecture a higher power limit.

Particularly promising is just how stable that 30 fps seems to be on the PS5 Pro. People often think about the average, but don't consider frame pacing and 1% lows. On those fronts, GTA 6 seems very well optimised.

Our Chris has spent 100 hours with the Playstation 5 version of GTA 6, and has come away with some very positive impressions. Here's hoping the PC release lives up to the hype, and that those of us on older rigs might be able to get in on the action without too many pricey upgrades.

Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born. Since then, Jacob's led a double-life as part-hardware geek, part-philosophy nerd, first working as a Hardware Writer for PCGamesN in 2020, then working towards a PhD in Philosophy for a few years while freelancing on the side for sites such as TechRadar, Pocket-lint, and yours truly, PC Gamer. Eventually, he gave up the ruthless mercenary life to join the world's #1 PC Gaming site full-time. It's definitely not an ego thing, he assures us.
